bookInfo.name: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance
bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第277卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 277.
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi Tongjian, Volume 277.

sentences.zh: 【後唐紀六】 起上章攝提格，盡玄黓執徐六月，凡二年有奇。

translations.literal: [Later Tang Annals 6] From Shangzhang Shetige through the sixth month of Xuanchi Zhixu; a little more than two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Later Tang, Part 6] From Shangzhang Shetige through the sixth month of Xuanchi Zhixu—a little more than two years in all.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之下長興元年（

translations.literal: Middle section, lower part, first year of Changxing of Emperor Mingzong, the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (
translations.idiomatic: First year of Changxing (930), middle and lower section of the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, styled the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (

sentences.zh: 庚寅，公元九三零年）

translations.literal: gengyin, corresponding to the year 930 CE).
translations.idiomatic: 930 CE, year gengyin).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，董璋遣兵築七寨於劍門。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Dong Zhang sent troops to build seven fortified camps at Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Dong Zhang sent troops to erect seven stockades at Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，孟知祥遣趙季良如梓州修好。

translations.literal: On the day xinsi, Meng Zhixiang sent Zhao Jiliang to Zizhou to restore friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, Meng Zhixiang dispatched Zhao Jiliang to Zizhou to renew amicable ties.

sentences.zh: 鴻臚少卿郭在徽奏請鑄當五千、三千、一千大錢；

translations.literal: Guo Zaichui, Vice Director of the Directorate of Guests, memorialized requesting the casting of large coins worth five thousand, three thousand, and one thousand cash each;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zaichui, Vice Director of the Directorate of Guests, petitioned to mint large coins denominated at five thousand, three thousand, and one thousand cash;

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其指虛為實，無識妄言，左遷衛尉少卿、同正。

translations.literal: the court, holding that he treated the insubstantial as real and spoke rashly without understanding, demoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud with the honorary concurrent title.
translations.idiomatic: the court judged his proposal hollow economics and ignorant presumption, and demoted him to Vice Director of the Imperial Stud with an honorary concurrent appointment.

sentences.zh: 吳徙平原王澈為德化王。

translations.literal: Wu transferred Prince Che of Pingyuan to be Prince of Dehua.
translations.idiomatic: Wu transferred Prince Che of Pingyuan to the title Prince of Dehua.

sentences.zh: 二月，乙未朔，趙季良還成都，謂孟知祥曰：「董公貪殘好勝，志大謀短，終為西川之患。」

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day yimao, Zhao Jiliang returned to Chengdu and said to Meng Zhixiang, "Lord Dong is greedy, cruel, and competitive; his ambitions are large but his plans short—he will ultimately be a calamity for Western Chuan."
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the new moon of yimao, Zhao Jiliang returned to Chengdu and told Meng Zhixiang, "Dong Zhang is greedy, brutal, and combative—bold in aim but shallow in design. In the end he will be a scourge upon Western Chuan."

sentences.zh: 都指揮使李仁罕、張業欲置宴召知祥；

translations.literal: The metropolitan commanders Li Renhan and Zhang Ye wished to hold a banquet and summon Zhixiang;
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan commanders Li Renhan and Zhang Ye planned a banquet to invite Zhixiang;

sentences.zh: 先二日，有尼告二將謀以宴日害知祥；

translations.literal: two days earlier a nun reported that the two generals plotted to harm Zhixiang on the day of the feast;
translations.idiomatic: two days before, a Buddhist nun warned that the two generals intended to kill Zhixiang at the banquet;

sentences.zh: 知祥詰之，無狀，丁酉，推始言者軍校都延昌、王行本，腰斬之。

translations.literal: Zhixiang interrogated them, but there was no evidence; on dingyou he traced the original accusers to the military officers Du Yanzhang and Wang Xingben and had them cut in two at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang questioned them, found nothing to support the charge, and on dingyou traced the rumor to the officers Du Yanzhang and Wang Xingben, who had started it; he had both executed by waist-cutting.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，就宴，盡去左右，獨詣仁罕第；

translations.literal: On wuxu he attended the banquet, dismissed all his attendants, and went alone to Renhan's residence;
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he went to the feast after dismissing every attendant and walked alone to Renhan's house;

sentences.zh: 仁罕叩頭流涕曰：「老兵惟盡死以報德。」

translations.literal: Renhan kowtowed with tears and said, "This old soldier can only exhaust his life to repay your virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Renhan kowtowed, weeping, and said, "These old troops will spend our lives to repay your grace."

sentences.zh: 由是諸將皆親附而服之。

translations.literal: Thereupon all the generals drew close to him in affection and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: From that day the commanders all drew near to him in loyalty and yielded to his authority.

sentences.zh: 壬子，孟知祥、董璋同上表言：「兩川聞朝廷於閬中建節，綿、遂益兵，無不憂恐。」

translations.literal: On renzi, Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang jointly submitted a memorial stating, "The Two Chuan, hearing that the court is establishing a military commission at Lang and reinforcing Mian and Sui, are without exception anxious and afraid."
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Meng Zhixiang and Dong Zhang jointly memorialized: "Both Chuan regions, learning that the court is setting up a command at Langzhou and reinforcing Mian and Sui, are filled with alarm."

sentences.zh: 上以詔書慰諭之。

translations.literal: The emperor responded with an edict of reassurance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered with an edict of comfort and reassurance.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，上祀圓丘，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On yimao the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the emperor offered sacrifice at the Round Mound, granted a general amnesty, and proclaimed a new reign era.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔節度使兼中書令李從曮入朝陪祀，三月，壬申，制徙從曮為宣武節度使。

translations.literal: Li Congying, military governor of Fengxiang and concurrent Grand Councilor, entered court to attend the rites; in the third month, on renshen, an order transferred Congying to be military governor of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congying, military governor of Fengxiang and concurrent Grand Councilor, came to court for the rites; in the third month, on renshen, he was ordered transferred to military governor of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，吳主立江都王璉為太子。

translations.literal: On guiyou the ruler of Wu installed Prince Lin of Jiangdu as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou the Wu ruler installed Prince Lin of Jiangdu as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 丙子，以宣徽使朱弘照為鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: On bingzi Zhu Hongzhao, Commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was appointed military governor of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi Zhu Hongzhao, Palace Secretariat commissioner, was made military governor of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 康福奏克保靜鎮，斬李匡賓。

translations.literal: Kang Fu reported the capture of Baojing prefecture and the execution of Li Kuangbin.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu reported that Baojing prefecture had been taken and Li Kuangbin beheaded.

sentences.zh: 復以安義為昭義軍。

translations.literal: Anyi was again made the Zhaoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Anyi circuit was restored to the name Zhaoyi Army.

sentences.zh: 帝將立曹淑妃為后，淑妃謂王德妃曰：「吾素病中煩，倦於接對，妹代我為之。」

translations.literal: The emperor was about to establish Consort Cao Shufei as empress; the consort said to Virtuous Consort Wang, "I have long suffered from internal vexation and am weary of receiving audiences—sister, take my place in this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to elevate Consort Cao to empress; she told Virtuous Consort Wang, "I have long been troubled by inner ailments and am weary of audiences—dear sister, stand in for me."

sentences.zh: 德妃曰：「中宮敵偶至尊，誰敢干之！」

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Wang said, "The central palace is the equal partner of the supreme sovereign—who would dare to intrude upon it!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang replied, "The empress is the sovereign's equal in the inner palace—who would dare usurp that place!"

sentences.zh: 庚寅，立淑妃為皇后。

translations.literal: On gengyin Shufei was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin the emperor installed her as empress nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 德妃事后恭謹，后亦憐之。

translations.literal: Virtuous Consort Wang served the empress with reverent care, and the empress also cherished her.
translations.idiomatic: Wang served the empress with respectful devotion, and the empress in turn treated her with affection.

sentences.zh: 初，王德妃因安重誨得進，常德之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wang Defei had advanced through An Chonghui and always deferred to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang had risen through An Chonghui's patronage and always honored him.

sentences.zh: 帝性儉約，及在位久，宮中用度稍侈，重誨每規諫。

translations.literal: The emperor's nature was frugal, but after he had been on the throne a long time the palace expenditures grew somewhat lavish, and Chonghui repeatedly admonished him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been frugal by nature, yet the longer he reigned the more the palace spending grew; Chonghui admonished him again and again.

sentences.zh: 妃取外庫錦造地衣，重誨切諫，引劉后為戒；

translations.literal: The consort took brocade from the outer storehouse to make a carpet; Chonghui remonstrated sharply and cited Empress Liu as a warning;
translations.idiomatic: When the consort took brocade from the outer treasury to weave a floor carpet, Chonghui remonstrated sternly, citing Empress Liu as a cautionary example;

sentences.zh: 妃由是怨之。

translations.literal: the consort therefore came to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: from that time the consort bore him a grudge.

sentences.zh: 高從誨遣使奉表詣吳，告以墳墓在中國，恐為唐所討，吳兵援之不及，謝絕之。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui sent envoys bearing a memorial to Wu, reporting that his ancestral tombs lay in China and that he feared Tang would attack and Wu troops could not arrive in time; Wu declined the overture.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui sent envoys with a memorial to Wu, explaining that his family tombs lay in Tang territory and that he feared a Tang punitive campaign before Wu forces could help; Wu refused him.

sentences.zh: 吳遣兵擊之，不克。

translations.literal: Wu sent troops to attack him but could not overcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent troops against him but failed to prevail.

sentences.zh: 董璋恐綿州刺史武虔裕窺其所為，夏，四月，甲午朔，表兼行軍司馬，囚之府廷。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang feared that Wu Qianyu, prefect of Mian, would spy on his actions; in summer, the fourth month, on the first day jiawu, he memorialized to add the concurrent post of army marshal and imprisoned Wu in the courtyard of his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang feared Mian prefect Wu Qianyu was watching his moves; in summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of jiawu he petitioned to take the concurrent title of army marshal and imprisoned Wu in his headquarters courtyard.

sentences.zh: 宣武節度使符習，自恃宿將，論議多抗安重誨，重誨求其過失，奏之，丁酉，詔習以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: Fu Xi, military governor of Xuanwu, relying on his status as a veteran commander, often opposed An Chonghui in discussion; Chonghui sought out his faults and memorialized them; on dingyou an edict ordered Xi to retire as Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xi of Xuanwu, trusting in his long service, often contradicted An Chonghui in council; Chonghui hunted for faults and reported them; on dingyou the emperor ordered Xi to retire with the title Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，加孟知祥兼中書令，夏魯奇同平章事。

translations.literal: On wuxu Meng Zhixiang was additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor, and Xia Luqi Associate Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Meng Zhixiang was given the additional title of Grand Councilor, and Xia Luqi was made Associate Councilor.

sentences.zh: 初，帝在真定，李從珂與安重誨飲酒爭言，從珂毆重誨，重誨走免；

translations.literal: Earlier, when the emperor was at Zhending, Li Congke and An Chonghui quarreled while drinking; Congke struck Chonghui, and Chonghui ran off and escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Long before, when the emperor was at Zhending, Li Congke and An Chonghui had quarreled over wine; Congke struck Chonghui, who fled and escaped injury;

sentences.zh: 既醒，悔謝，重誨終銜之。

translations.literal: when sober Congke regretted it and apologized, but Chonghui bore a grudge to the end.
translations.idiomatic: when sober Congke repented and apologized, yet Chonghui never forgave him.

sentences.zh: 至是，重誨用事，自皇子從榮、從厚皆敬事不暇。

translations.literal: By this time Chonghui held power, and even the princes Congrong and Conghou could scarcely keep up with honoring him.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Chonghui held power, even the princes Congrong and Conghou could barely keep pace with showing him deference.

sentences.zh: 時從珂為河中節度使、同平章事，重誨屢短之於帝，帝不聽。

translations.literal: At this time Congke was military governor of Hezhong and Associate Councilor; Chonghui repeatedly spoke ill of him to the emperor, but the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Congke was then military governor of Hezhong and Associate Councilor; Chonghui slandered him to the emperor again and again, but the emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 重誨乃矯以帝命諭河東牙內指揮使楊彥溫使逐之。

translations.literal: Chonghui then forged the emperor's command and instructed Yang Yanwen, commander of the Hedong inner guard, to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui then forged an imperial order and told Yang Yanwen, commander of the Hedong inner guard, to drive Congke out.

sentences.zh: 是日，從珂出城閱馬，彥溫勒兵閉門拒之，從珂使人扣門詰之曰：「吾將汝厚，何為如是？」

translations.literal: That day Congke went outside the city to review the horses; Yanwen led troops and shut the gates to bar him; Congke sent someone to knock on the gate and demand, "I have treated you generously—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: That day Congke rode out to inspect the horses; Yanwen mobilized his men and sealed the gates against him. Congke sent a man to knock and demand, "I have treated you well—why do this?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「彥溫非敢負恩，受樞密院宣耳。

translations.literal: He replied, "Yanwen does not dare betray your grace—I received an order from the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanwen answered, "I do not dare betray your kindness; I act on an order from the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 請公入朝。」

translations.literal: I ask my lord to enter court."
translations.idiomatic: Please, my lord, go to court."

sentences.zh: 從珂止於虞鄉，遣使以狀聞。

translations.literal: Congke halted at Yuxiang and sent a messenger to report the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Congke stopped at Yuxiang and sent a messenger to lay the matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 使者至，壬寅，帝問重誨曰：「彥溫安得此言？」

translations.literal: When the messenger arrived, on renyin the emperor asked Chonghui, "How could Yanwen say such a thing?"
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger arrived, on renyin the emperor asked Chonghui, "How could Yanwen speak so?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「此奸人妄言耳，宜速討之。」

translations.literal: He replied, "This is the wild talk of a villain—he should be punished at once."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui answered, "Wicked men lie—that is all. He should be struck down at once."

sentences.zh: 帝疑之，欲誘致彥溫訊其事，除彥溫絳州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious and wished to lure Yanwen in to question him about the affair; he appointed Yanwen prefect of Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was doubtful and wanted to lure Yanwen in for questioning; he appointed Yanwen prefect of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 重誨固請發兵擊之，乃命西都留守索自通、步軍都指揮使藥彥稠將兵討之。

translations.literal: Chonghui firmly requested that troops be sent to attack; thereupon the emperor ordered Suo Zitong, defender of the Western Capital, and Yao Yanchou, commander of the foot soldiers, to lead troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui pressed for military action, and the emperor ordered Suo Zitong, defender of the Western Capital, and Yao Yanchou, infantry commander, to campaign against Yanwen.

sentences.zh: 帝令彥稠必生致彥溫，吾欲面訊之。

translations.literal: The emperor told Yanchou that Yanwen must be taken alive—"I wish to question him face to face."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yanchou he must capture Yanwen alive: "I want to question him in person."

sentences.zh: 召從珂詣洛陽。

translations.literal: He summoned Congke to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Congke to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 從珂知為重誨所構，馳入自明。

translations.literal: Congke knew he had been framed by Chonghui and galloped in to clear himself.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Chonghui had framed him, Congke raced to the capital to plead his innocence.

sentences.zh: 加安重誨兼中書令。

translations.literal: An Chonghui was additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui was given the additional title of Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 李從珂至洛陽，上責之使歸第，絕朝請。

translations.literal: When Li Congke reached Luoyang, the emperor reproached him and sent him back to his residence, cutting off his attendance at court.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Congke reached Luoyang, the emperor rebuked him, ordered him home, and barred him from court audiences.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，索自通等拔河中，斬楊彥溫，癸丑，傳首來獻。

translations.literal: On xinhai Suo Zitong and others captured Hezhong and beheaded Yang Yanwen; on guichou the head was sent in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Suo Zitong took Hezhong and beheaded Yang Yanwen; on guichou the head was presented at court.

sentences.zh: 上怒藥彥稠不生致，深責之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry that Yao Yanchou had not taken him alive and rebuked him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious that Yao Yanchou had not captured Yanwen alive and scolded him harshly.

sentences.zh: 安重誨諷馮道、趙鳳奏從珂失守，宜加罪。

translations.literal: An Chonghui prompted Feng Dao and Zhao Feng to memorialize that Congke had failed in his post and ought to be punished.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui urged Feng Dao and Zhao Feng to memorialize that Congke had lost his command and deserved punishment.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「吾兒為奸黨所傾，未明曲直，公輩何為發此言，意不欲置之人間邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said, "My son has been overthrown by schemers; right and wrong are not yet clear—why do you gentlemen speak thus? Do you mean that you do not wish to leave him among the living?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "My son has been wronged by schemers before anyone knows who is right—why do you press this? Do you mean you want him dead?

sentences.zh: 此皆非公輩之意也。」

translations.literal: This is not what you gentlemen truly intend."
translations.idiomatic: That is not what you truly mean."

sentences.zh: 二人惶恐而退。

translations.literal: The two men withdrew in fear.
translations.idiomatic: The two men withdrew in terror.

sentences.zh: 它日，趙鳳又言之，上不應。

translations.literal: Another day Zhao Feng spoke of it again; the emperor did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: On another day Zhao Feng raised it again; the emperor gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 明日，重誨自言之，上曰：「朕昔為小校，家貧，賴此小兒拾馬糞自贍，以至今日為天子，曾不能庇之邪！

translations.literal: The next day Chonghui spoke of it himself; the emperor said, "In the past I was a petty officer, my household poor; I relied on this boy gathering horse dung to support himself, until today I became Son of Heaven—can I not even shelter him!
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chonghui brought it up himself. The emperor said, "When I was only a junior officer, my family was poor. This boy gathered horse dung to keep himself fed until I became emperor—can I not even protect him now?

sentences.zh: 卿欲如何處之於卿為便？」

translations.literal: How would you, minister, dispose of him in a way convenient to you?"
translations.idiomatic: Tell me how you would dispose of him to suit yourself."

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「陛下父子之間，臣何敢言！

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "Between Your Majesty and your son, how would your servant dare to speak!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "Between father and son, how dare a subject speak!

sentences.zh: 惟陛下裁之！」

translations.literal: I ask only that Your Majesty decide!"
translations.idiomatic: I leave it entirely to Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「使閒居私第亦可矣，何復言！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Let him live in retirement in his private residence—that is enough; why speak further!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Let him live quietly at home—that is enough. Say no more."

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以索自通為河中節度使。

translations.literal: On bingchen Suo Zitong was made military governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Suo Zitong was appointed military governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 自通至鎮，承重誨旨，籍軍府甲仗數上之，以為從珂私造，賴王德妃居中保護，從珂由是得免。

translations.literal: When Zitong reached his post he followed Chonghui's intent, inventoried the armaments of the military headquarters and reported the numbers upward, alleging that Congke had manufactured them privately; only through Virtuous Consort Wang's intercession at court was Congke thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: At his post Zitong followed Chonghui's wishes, inventoried the commandery's arms and armor, and reported them as proof that Congke had armed himself in secret; only Wang Defei's mediation at court saved Congke from ruin.

sentences.zh: 士大夫不敢與從珂往來；

translations.literal: Literati and officials did not dare to associate with Congke;
translations.idiomatic: Officials dared not visit Congke;

sentences.zh: 惟禮部郎中史館修撰呂琦居相近，時往見之，從珂每月奏請，皆咨琦而後行。

translations.literal: only Lü Qi, Director in the Ministry of Rites and drafter at the History Office, lived nearby and from time to time visited him; each month Congke's memorials and petitions were all submitted only after consulting Qi.
translations.idiomatic: only Lü Qi of the Ministry of Rites, who also served as a history drafter and lived nearby, still called on him from time to time; Congke consulted Qi before sending each month's memorials.

sentences.zh: 戊午，帝加尊號曰聖明神武文德恭孝皇帝。

translations.literal: On wuwu the emperor added the honorific title Sagacious, Illuminated, Divine, Martial, Civilly Virtuous, Reverent, and Filial Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the emperor took the augmented title Sagacious, Illuminated, Divine, Martial, Civilly Virtuous, Reverent, and Filial Emperor.

sentences.zh: 安重誨言昭義節度使王建立過魏州有搖眾之語，五月，丙寅，制以太傅致仕。

translations.literal: An Chonghui reported that Wang Jianli, military governor of Zhaoyi, had uttered words at Weizhou that would shake the multitude; in the fifth month, on bingyin, an order directed him to retire as Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui accused Zhaoyi governor Wang Jianli of seditious talk while passing through Weizhou; in the fifth month, on bingyin, he was ordered to retire as Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 董璋閱集民兵，皆剪髮黥面，復於劍門北置永定關，布列烽火。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang reviewed and assembled the militia, all of whom had their hair cropped and faces tattooed; he also set up Yongding Pass north of Jianmen and deployed beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang mustered the militia, had them crop their hair and tattoo their faces, built Yongding Pass north of Jianmen, and lined the heights with beacon fires.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥累表請割雲安等十三鹽監隸西川，以鹽直贍寧江屯兵，辛卯，許之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang repeatedly memorialized requesting that thirteen salt offices including Yun'an be assigned to Western Chuan, using salt revenue to support the garrison troops at Ningjiang; on xinmao this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang repeatedly asked that thirteen salt offices, including Yun'an, be placed under Western Chuan so salt profits could pay the Ningjiang garrison; on xinmao the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 六月，癸已朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the new moon of guisi, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，敕防禦、團練使、刺史、行軍司馬、節度副使，自今皆自朝廷除之，諸道無得奏薦。

translations.literal: On xinhai an edict declared that defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, army marshals, and deputy military governors would henceforth all be appointed by the court, and the various circuits might not memorialize recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ruled that defense commissioners, training commissioners, prefects, army marshals, and deputy governors would hereafter all be appointed from the capital, and no circuit might recommend its own candidates.

sentences.zh: 董璋遣兵掠遂、閬鎮戍，秋，七月，戊辰，兩川以朝廷繼遣兵屯遂、閬，復有論奏，自是東北商旅少敢入蜀。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang sent troops to plunder the garrison posts of Sui and Lang; in autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen, the Two Chuan again submitted memorials of protest because the court had continued to station troops at Sui and Lang; from this time few merchants from the northeast dared enter Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang raided the garrisons of Sui and Lang; in autumn, the seventh month, on wuchen both Chuan regions memorialized again because the court kept troops at Sui and Lang; thereafter few northeastern traders dared enter Shu.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙未，捧聖軍使李行德、十將張儉引告密人邊彥溫告「安重誨發兵，雲欲自討淮南；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on yimao, Li Xingde, commissioner of the Paladin Army, and Commander Zhang Jian of the Ten brought the informant Bian Yanwen to report that "An Chonghui has mobilized troops, saying he intends to campaign against Huainan himself;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yimao, Paladin Army commissioner Li Xingde and commander Zhang Jian presented the informer Bian Yanwen, who claimed that "An Chonghui has raised troops, saying he will personally campaign against Huainan;

sentences.zh: 又引占相者問命。」

translations.literal: and also brought in diviners who read fortunes to inquire about his fate."
translations.idiomatic: and had also consulted fortune-tellers about his destiny."

sentences.zh: 帝以問侍衛都指揮使安從進、藥彥稠，二人曰：「此奸人欲離間陛下勳舊耳。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the guard commanders An Congjin and Yao Yanchou; the two said, "These are villains who wish to drive a wedge between Your Majesty and your meritorious veterans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked guard commanders An Congjin and Yao Yanchou; both said, "These are villains trying to set Your Majesty against your old companions in arms.

sentences.zh: 重誨事陛下三十年，幸而富貴，何苦謀反！

translations.literal: Chonghui has served Your Majesty for thirty years and has by good fortune grown wealthy—why would he bitterly plot rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui has served you thirty years and is wealthy at last—why would he rebel now!

sentences.zh: 臣等請以宗族保之。」

translations.literal: Your servants ask to guarantee him with our clans."
translations.idiomatic: We pledge our families on his loyalty."

sentences.zh: 帝乃斬彥溫，召重誨慰撫之，君臣相泣。

translations.literal: The emperor then beheaded Yanwen, summoned Chonghui to comfort him, and ruler and minister wept together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor beheaded Yanwen, summoned Chonghui to reassure him, and emperor and minister wept together.

sentences.zh: 以前忠武節度使張延朗行工部尚書，充三司使。

translations.literal: The former military governor of Zhongwu, Zhang Yanlang, was appointed acting Minister of Works and made Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: Former Zhongwu military governor Zhang Yanlang was appointed acting Minister of Works and Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 三司使之名自此始。

translations.literal: The title Commissioner of the Three Departments began from this time.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Commissioner of the Three Departments dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥以海州都指揮使王傳拯有威名，得士心，值團練使陳宣罷歸，知誥許以傳拯代之；

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhihao, finding that Wang Chuanzhen, metropolitan commander of Haizhou, had a formidable reputation and won the hearts of the troops, and that Regiment Trainer Chen Xuan was returning after dismissal, promised Chuanzhen the post in Xuan's place;
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhihao saw that Haizhou commander Wang Chuanzhen was formidable and beloved by the troops; when regiment trainer Chen Xuan was recalled, Zhihao promised Chuanzhen the post;

sentences.zh: 既而復遣宣還海州，征傳拯還江都。

translations.literal: but afterward he again sent Xuan back to Haizhou and summoned Chuanzhen back to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: then he sent Xuan back to Haizhou after all and recalled Chuanzhen to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 傳拯怒，以為宣毀之，己亥，帥麾下入辭宣。

translations.literal: Chuanzhen was enraged, believing Xuan had slandered him; on jihai he led his personal guard in to take leave of Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzhen, furious and convinced Xuan had ruined him, led his personal guard on jihai to bid Xuan farewell.

sentences.zh: 因斬宣，焚掠城郭，帥其眾五千來奔。

translations.literal: Thereupon he slew Xuan, burned and plundered the city, and led his five thousand men to defect.
translations.idiomatic: He killed Xuan on the spot, burned and looted the city, and defected with five thousand men.

sentences.zh: 知誥曰：「是吾過也。」

translations.literal: Zhihao said, "This is my fault."
translations.idiomatic: Zhihao said, "This was my mistake."

sentences.zh: 免其妻子。

translations.literal: He exempted Chuanzhen's wife and children from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He spared Chuanzhen's wife and children.

sentences.zh: 漣水制置使王巖將兵入海州，以巖為威衛大將軍，知海州。

translations.literal: Wang Yan, intendant of Lianshui, led troops into Haizhou; Yan was made Grand General of the Majestic Guard and given charge of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lianshui intendant Wang Yan marched into Haizhou; Yan was made Grand General of the Majestic Guard with charge of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 傳拯，綰之子也，其季父輿為光州刺史。

translations.literal: Chuanzhen was the son of Wang Chuo; his younger uncle Yu was prefect of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzhen was Wang Chuo's son; his uncle Yu was prefect of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 傳拯遣間使持書至光州，輿執之以聞，因求罷歸；

translations.literal: Chuanzhen sent a secret messenger bearing a letter to Guang; Yu seized him and reported it, and thereby requested to be relieved and return;
translations.idiomatic: Chuanzhen sent a secret messenger with a letter to Guangzhou; Yu arrested the man and reported upward, then asked to resign and return home;

sentences.zh: 知誥以輿為控鶴都虞候。

translations.literal: Zhihao appointed Yu deputy commander of the Crane-Control Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihao made Yu deputy commander of the Crane-Control Guard.

sentences.zh: 時政在徐氏，典兵宿衛者尤難其人，知誥以輿重厚慎密，故用之。

translations.literal: At that time political power lay with the Xu clan, and finding men to command troops and guard the palace was especially difficult; Zhihao used Yu because he was grave, steady, and discreet.
translations.idiomatic: Power then rested with the Xu clan, and trustworthy commanders for the palace guard were hard to find; Zhihao valued Yu for his gravity and discretion.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，趙鳳奏：「切聞近有奸人，誣陷大臣，搖國柱石，行之未盡。」

translations.literal: On renyin Zhao Feng memorialized, "I have urgently heard that recently villains have falsely accused great ministers and shaken the pillars of the state—the matter has not yet been fully carried through."
translations.idiomatic: On renyin Zhao Feng memorialized: "I have just learned that villains have lately framed great ministers and shaken the state's pillars—the purge is not yet finished."

sentences.zh: 帝乃收李行德、張儉，皆族之。

translations.literal: The emperor then arrested Li Xingde and Zhang Jian and executed their entire clans.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then seized Li Xingde and Zhang Jian and executed their whole families.

sentences.zh: 立皇子從榮為秦王；

translations.literal: Prince Congrong was established as Prince of Qin;
translations.idiomatic: Prince Congrong was installed as Prince of Qin;

sentences.zh: 丙辰，立從厚為宋王。

translations.literal: On bingchen Conghou was established as Prince of Song.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Prince Conghou was installed as Prince of Song.

sentences.zh: 董璋之子光業為宮苑使，在洛陽，璋與書曰：「朝廷割吾支郡為節鎮，屯兵三千，是殺我必矣。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang's son Guangye was commissioner of the palace parks and was in Luoyang; Zhang wrote to him, "The court has carved off my subordinate prefectures to make military commissions and stationed three thousand troops—that is surely to kill me.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang's son Guangye served as palace parks commissioner in Luoyang. Zhang wrote him: "The court has split off my subordinate districts as separate commands and posted three thousand troops—they mean to destroy me.

sentences.zh: 汝見樞要為吾言：如朝廷更發一騎入斜谷，吾必反！

translations.literal: When you see the chief ministers, speak for me: if the court sends even one more rider into Xiegu, I will certainly rebel!
translations.idiomatic: Tell the chief ministers for me: if the court sends one more soldier through Xiegu Pass, I will rebel!

sentences.zh: 與汝訣矣。」

translations.literal: This is my farewell to you."
translations.idiomatic: This is farewell between us."

sentences.zh: 光業以書示樞密承旨李虔徽。

translations.literal: Guangye showed the letter to Li Qianhui, chief drafter at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangye showed the letter to Li Qianhui, chief drafter at the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，朝廷又遣別將荀鹹乂將兵戍閬州，光業謂虔徽曰：「此兵未至，吾父必反。

translations.literal: Before long the court again sent the deputy commander Xun Xianyi to lead troops to garrison Langzhou; Guangye said to Qianhui, "Before these troops arrive, my father will certainly rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the court sent deputy commander Xun Xianyi to garrison Langzhou. Guangye told Qianhui, "Before those troops even arrive, my father will rebel.

sentences.zh: 吾不敢自愛，恐煩朝廷調發，願止此兵，吾父保無他。」

translations.literal: I do not dare spare myself, fearing to trouble the court with mobilization; I ask only that these troops be halted, and my father will surely keep the peace."
translations.idiomatic: I do not value my own life, but I fear burdening the court with a campaign—please halt these troops, and my father will remain loyal."

sentences.zh: 虔徽以告安重誨，重誨不從。

translations.literal: Qianhui reported this to An Chonghui, but Chonghui would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Qianhui reported this to An Chonghui, who refused.

sentences.zh: 璋聞之，遂反。

translations.literal: When Zhang heard of it, he rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang learned of this, he rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 利、閬、遂三鎮以聞，且言已聚兵將攻三鎮。

translations.literal: The three prefectures of Li, Lang, and Sui reported it and also stated that he had already gathered troops to attack the three commands.
translations.idiomatic: The Li, Lang, and Sui commands reported the revolt and warned that Zhang had already massed troops to attack them.

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「臣久知其如此，陛下含容不討耳。」

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "Your servant long knew he would come to this; Your Majesty has borne with him and not punished him."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "I have long known he would do this; Your Majesty has only been forbearing."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我不負人，人負我則討之！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I do not fail others; when others fail me, then I punish them!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I do not wrong others—when others wrong me, I strike back!"

sentences.zh: 九月，癸亥，西川進奏官蘇願白孟知祥云：「朝廷欲大發兵討兩川。」

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guihai, Su Yuan, memorial envoy of Western Chuan, informed Meng Zhixiang, "The court intends to mobilize a great army to attack the Two Chuan."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guihai, Western Chuan memorial envoy Su Yuan told Meng Zhixiang, "The court plans a major campaign against both Chuan regions."

sentences.zh: 知祥謀於副使趙季良，季良請以東川兵先取遂、閬，然後並兵守劍門，則大軍雖來，吾無內顧之憂矣。

translations.literal: Zhixiang consulted with his deputy Zhao Jiliang; Jiliang proposed that Eastern Chuan troops first take Sui and Lang, then combine forces to hold Jianmen—then even if a great army came, they would have no worry about threats from within.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang consulted deputy Zhao Jiliang, who urged using Eastern Chuan forces to seize Sui and Lang first, then unite to hold Jianmen Pass—so even if a great northern army came, they need not fear attack from behind.

sentences.zh: 知祥從之，遣使約董璋同舉兵。

translations.literal: Zhixiang agreed and sent envoys to arrange with Dong Zhang to raise troops together.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang agreed and sent envoys to coordinate a joint rising with Dong Zhang.

sentences.zh: 璋移繳利、閬、遂三鎮，數其離間朝廷，引兵擊閬州。

translations.literal: Zhang issued a proclamation to the three commands of Li, Lang, and Sui, enumerating their sowing division against the court, and led troops to attack Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang issued a formal summons to the Li, Lang, and Sui commands, accusing them of driving a wedge between the court and the provinces, and marched on Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚午，知祥以都指揮使李仁罕為行營都部署，漢州刺史趙廷隱副之，簡州刺史張業為先鋒指揮使，將兵三萬攻遂州；

translations.literal: On gengwu Zhixiang appointed metropolitan commander Li Renhan as overall camp commander, Zhao Tingyin, prefect of Han, as his deputy, and Zhang Ye, prefect of Jian, as vanguard commander, leading thirty thousand troops to attack Suizhou;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Zhixiang made Li Renhan overall camp commander, with Han prefect Zhao Tingyin as deputy and Jian prefect Zhang Ye as vanguard, leading thirty thousand men against Suizhou;

sentences.zh: 別將牙內都指揮使侯弘實、先登指揮使孟思恭將兵四千會璋攻閬州。

translations.literal: the separate commanders Hou Hongshi, metropolitan inner guard commander, and Meng Sigong, first-assault commander, led four thousand troops to join Zhang in attacking Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: separate commanders Hou Hongshi and Meng Sigong led four thousand men to join Zhang's assault on Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 安重誨久專大權，中外惡之者眾；

translations.literal: An Chonghui had long monopolized great power, and many within and without the court hated him;
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui had held power for years, and many at court and beyond resented him;

sentences.zh: 王德妃及武德使孟漢瓊浸用事，數短重誨於上。

translations.literal: Wang Defei and Meng Hanqiong, commissioner of Wude, gradually gained influence and repeatedly spoke ill of Chonghui to the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Defei and Wude commissioner Meng Hanqiong gradually gained influence and repeatedly slandered Chonghui to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 重誨內憂懼，表解機務，上曰：「朕無間於卿，誣罔者朕既誅之矣，卿何為爾？」

translations.literal: Chonghui was inwardly anxious and fearful and memorialized to resign from state affairs; the emperor said, "I have no estrangement from you; I have already executed those who slandered you—why act thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui grew fearful and asked to resign from state affairs. The emperor said, "I bear you no ill will—I have already executed your accusers. Why do this?"

sentences.zh: 甲戌，重誨復面奏曰：「臣以寒賤，致位至此，忽為人誣以反，非陛下至明，臣無種矣。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Chonghui again addressed the throne in person: "Your servant, from humble and low origins, rose to this position; suddenly men falsely accused me of rebellion—had Your Majesty not been supremely clear-sighted, your servant would have left no descendants.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Chonghui pleaded in person again: "I rose from poverty to this height, only to be accused of treason—had Your Majesty not been so clear-sighted, my line would have been extinguished.

sentences.zh: 由臣才薄任重，恐終不能鎮浮言，願賜一鎮以全餘生。」

translations.literal: Because your servant's talent is thin while his burden is heavy, I fear I cannot in the end suppress loose talk; I ask to be granted one military commission to preserve the remainder of my life."
translations.idiomatic: My abilities are too slight for this burden; I fear I cannot silence the rumors. Grant me a post in the provinces so I may live out my days in peace."

sentences.zh: 上不許；

translations.literal: The emperor did not consent;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused;

sentences.zh: 重誨求之不已，上怒曰：「聽卿去，朕不患無人！」

translations.literal: Chonghui pressed without cease; the emperor said in anger, "Go if you wish—I am not troubled for lack of men!"
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui pressed on without cease until the emperor snapped, "Go then—I am not short of men!"

sentences.zh: 前成德節度使范延光勸上留重誨，且曰：「重誨去，誰能代之？」

translations.literal: The former military governor of Chengde, Fan Yanguang, urged the emperor to retain Chonghui and said, "If Chonghui goes, who can replace him?"
translations.idiomatic: Former Chengde governor Fan Yanguang urged the emperor to keep Chonghui: "If he goes, who can replace him?"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿豈不可？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Could you not do it?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Could you not do it yourself?"

sentences.zh: 延光曰：「臣受驅策日淺，且才不逮重誨，何敢當此？」

translations.literal: Yanguang said, "Your servant has served at Your Majesty's command only a short time, and my talent does not reach Chonghui's—how would I dare undertake this?"
translations.idiomatic: Yanguang said, "I have served you only briefly, and my talent falls far short of Chonghui's—how could I dare take his place?"

sentences.zh: 上遣孟漢瓊詣中書議重誨事，馮道曰：「諸公果愛安令，宜解其樞務為便。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to discuss Chonghui's case; Feng Dao said, "If you gentlemen truly care for Director An, it would be best to relieve him of his bureau duties."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Meng Hanqiong to the Secretariat to discuss Chonghui's case. Feng Dao said, "If you truly value Director An, you should relieve him of his bureau duties."

sentences.zh: 趙鳳曰：「公失言。」

translations.literal: Zhao Feng said, "Sir, you misspeak."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng said, "You speak wrongly."

sentences.zh: 乃奏大臣不可輕動。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized that great ministers must not be lightly displaced.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that great ministers must not be removed lightly.

sentences.zh: 東川兵至閬州，諸將皆曰：「重璋久蓄反謀，以金帛啖其士卒，銳氣不可當，宜深溝高壘以挫之，不過旬日，大軍至，賊自走矣。」

translations.literal: When Eastern Chuan troops reached Langzhou, all the generals said, "Zhang has long harbored rebellious designs and uses gold and silk to feed his soldiers; their keen spirit cannot be withstood—we should dig deep ditches and raise high ramparts to blunt them; in no more than ten days the great army will arrive and the rebels will flee of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: When Eastern Chuan troops reached Langzhou, the generals all said, "Zhang has plotted rebellion for years and buys his soldiers with gold and silk. Their spirit is too fierce to meet head-on—we should entrench behind deep ditches and high walls until the main army arrives in ten days and the rebels scatter."

sentences.zh: 李仁矩曰：「蜀兵懦弱，安能當我精卒！」

translations.literal: Li Renju said, "Shu troops are weak—how can they withstand our elite soldiers!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Renju said, "Shu soldiers are cowards—how can they stand against our elite troops!"

sentences.zh: 遂出戰，兵未交而潰歸。

translations.literal: He therefore went out to give battle, but before the armies had clashed his troops collapsed and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: He marched out to fight, but his army broke and fled before the lines even met.

sentences.zh: 董璋晝夜攻之，庚辰，城陷，殺仁矩，滅其族。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang attacked day and night; on gengchen the city fell, Renju was killed, and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang assaulted day and night; on gengchen the city fell. He killed Renju and exterminated his clan.

sentences.zh: 初，璋為梁將，指揮使姚洪嘗隸麾下，至是，將兵千人戍閬州；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhang was a Liang general, the commander Yao Hong had once served under him; at this time he was garrisoning Langzhou with a thousand troops;
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, when Zhang served Liang, commander Yao Hong had been under his command; now Hong garrisoned Langzhou with a thousand men;

sentences.zh: 璋密以書誘之，洪投諸廁。

translations.literal: Zhang secretly sent a letter to entice him; Hong threw it into the privy.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang secretly sent him a letter of enticement; Hong threw it down the latrine.

sentences.zh: 城陷，璋執洪而讓之曰：「吾自行間獎拔汝，今日何相負？」

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhang seized Hong and reproached him: "I myself raised you up from the ranks—how do you fail me today?"
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhang seized Hong and demanded, "I promoted you from the ranks myself—how do you repay me thus?"

sentences.zh: 洪曰：「老賊！

translations.literal: Hong said, "Old villain!
translations.idiomatic: Hong cried, "You old villain!

sentences.zh: 汝昔為李氏奴，掃馬糞，得臠炙，感恩無窮。

translations.literal: In the past you were a slave of the Li clan, sweeping horse dung; when you got a scrap of roasted meat your gratitude knew no end.
translations.idiomatic: You were once the Li family's slave, shoveling horse dung—a scrap of roasted meat and you were grateful forever.

sentences.zh: 今天子用汝為節度使，何負於汝而反邪？

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven made you a military governor—how has he failed you that you rebel?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven made you a military governor—what wrong did he do you that you rebel?

sentences.zh: 汝猶負天子，吾受汝何恩，而雲相負哉！

translations.literal: You still fail the Son of Heaven—what grace did I receive from you, that you speak of my failing you!
translations.idiomatic: You betray the Son of Heaven—what debt do I owe you that you speak of betrayal?

sentences.zh: 汝奴材，固無恥；

translations.literal: You are slave material and naturally shameless;
translations.idiomatic: You were born a slave and know no shame;

sentences.zh: 吾義士，豈忍為汝所為乎！

translations.literal: I am a man of righteousness—how could I bear to do as you do!
translations.idiomatic: I am a man of honor—how could I stoop to your deeds!

sentences.zh: 吾寧為天子死，不能與人奴並生！」

translations.literal: I would rather die for the Son of Heaven than live alongside a man's slave!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die for the emperor than live beside a slave like you!"

sentences.zh: 璋怒，然鑊於前，令壯士十人刲其肉自啖之，洪至死罵不絕聲。

translations.literal: Zhang was enraged, heated a cauldron before him, and ordered ten strong men to slice his flesh for themselves to eat; Hong cursed without cease until death.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang in fury set a cauldron boiling before him and had ten strong men carve Hong's flesh and eat it; Hong cursed without cease until he died.

sentences.zh: 帝置洪二子於近衛，厚給其家。

translations.literal: The emperor placed Hong's two sons in the close guard and richly provided for his family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor enrolled Hong's two sons in the palace guard and richly provided for his family.

sentences.zh: 甲申，以范延光為樞密使，安重誨如故。

translations.literal: On jiashen Fan Yanguang was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs; An Chonghui remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Fan Yanguang was appointed military affairs commissioner; An Chonghui kept his post.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，下制削董璋官爵，興兵討之。

translations.literal: On bingxu an edict was issued stripping Dong Zhang of rank and titles and raising troops to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu an edict stripped Dong Zhang of rank and title and ordered troops raised against him.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以孟知祥兼西南面供饋使。

translations.literal: On dinghai Meng Zhixiang was additionally made commissioner for supply on the southwestern front.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Meng Zhixiang was additionally made southwestern supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以天雄節度石敬瑭為東川行營都招討使，以夏魯奇為之副。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang, military governor of Tianxiong, was made overall campaign commander of the Eastern Chuan field army, with Xia Luqi as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxiong governor Shi Jingtang was made overall commander of the Eastern Chuan campaign, with Xia Luqi as deputy.

sentences.zh: 璋使孟思恭分兵攻集州，思恭輕進，敗歸；

translations.literal: Zhang sent Meng Sigong to divide troops and attack Jizhou; Sigong advanced rashly, was defeated, and returned;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang sent Meng Sigong to attack Jizhou; Sigong advanced recklessly, was beaten, and retreated;

sentences.zh: 璋怒，遣還成都，知祥免其官。

translations.literal: Zhang was angry and sent him back to Chengdu; Zhixiang stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang in anger sent him back to Chengdu; Zhixiang removed him from office.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以石敬瑭權知東川事。

translations.literal: On wuzi Shi Jingtang was made acting administrator of Eastern Chuan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Shi Jingtang was given acting charge of Eastern Chuan affairs.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以右武衛上將軍王思同為西都留守兼行營馬步都虞候，為伐蜀前鋒。

translations.literal: On gengyin Wang Sitong, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, was made defender of the Western Capital and concurrent chief adjutant of horse and foot in the field army, as vanguard for the campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wang Sitong, Grand General of the Right Martial Guard, was made defender of the Western Capital and chief adjutant of the campaign army, vanguard for the Shu expedition.

sentences.zh: 漢主遣其將梁克貞、李守鄜攻交州，拔之，執靜海節度使曲承美以歸，以其將李進守交州。

translations.literal: The ruler of Han sent his generals Liang Kezhen and Li Shouzhen to attack Jiaozhou, captured it, seized the Jinghai military governor Qu Chengmei and brought him back, and left his general Li Jin to guard Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Han ruler sent generals Liang Kezhen and Li Shouzhen against Jiaozhou, took the city, captured Jinghai governor Qu Chengmei, and left general Li Jin to hold Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸巳，李仁罕圍遂州，夏魯奇嬰城固守；

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on guisi, Li Renhan besieged Suizhou; Xia Luqi held the city and defended stubbornly;
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on guisi, Li Renhan besieged Suizhou while Xia Luqi held the walls;

sentences.zh: 孟知祥命都押牙高敬柔帥資州義軍二萬人築長城環之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang ordered the chief adjutant Gao Jingrou to lead twenty thousand volunteer troops from Zizhou to build a long wall encircling it.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang ordered chief adjutant Gao Jingrou to lead twenty thousand Zizhou militia in building a circumvallation around the city.

sentences.zh: 魯奇遣馬軍都指揮使康文通出戰，文通聞閬州陷，遂以其眾降於仁罕。

translations.literal: Luqi sent the cavalry commander Kang Wentong out to give battle; when Wentong heard that Langzhou had fallen, he led his troops to surrender to Renhan.
translations.idiomatic: Luqi sent cavalry commander Kang Wentong to fight; learning Langzhou had fallen, Wentong surrendered his force to Renhan.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，董璋引兵趣利州，遇雨，糧運不繼，還閬州。

translations.literal: On wuxu Dong Zhang led troops toward Lizhou; they met rain and grain transport could not keep up, so he returned to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Dong Zhang marched toward Lizhou, but rain disrupted his supply lines and he withdrew to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 知祥聞之，驚曰：「比破閬中，正欲逕取利州，其帥不武，必望風遁去。

translations.literal: When Zhixiang heard of it he said in alarm, "Having just taken Langzhong, I had intended to go straight to Lizhou; its commander is not martial and would surely flee at the first wind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang was alarmed: "With Langzhong just taken, I meant to strike straight for Lizhou—the commander there is no fighter and would surely flee.

sentences.zh: 吾獲其倉廩，據漫天之險，北軍終不能西救武信。

translations.literal: If we seize his granaries and hold the peril of Mantian, the northern army in the end cannot rescue Wuxin from the west.
translations.idiomatic: We would seize his stores, hold the Mantian heights, and the northern army could never relieve Wuxin from the west.

sentences.zh: 今董公僻處閬州，遠棄劍閣，非計也。」

translations.literal: Now Lord Dong sits remote at Langzhou, abandoning Jian'ge far behind—this is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: Now Dong sits idle at Langzhou, leaving Jian'ge far behind—that is no strategy."

sentences.zh: 欲遣兵三千助守劍門；

translations.literal: He wished to send three thousand troops to help guard Jianmen;
translations.idiomatic: He offered three thousand men to help hold Jianmen Pass;

sentences.zh: 璋固辭曰：「此已有備。」

translations.literal: Zhang firmly declined, saying, "That place is already prepared."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang refused firmly: "It is already defended."

sentences.zh: 錢鏐因朝廷冊閩王使都裴羽還，附表引咎；

translations.literal: Qian Liu, because the court's envoy Pei Yu, who had come to invest the King of Min, was returning, attached a memorial acknowledging fault;
translations.idiomatic: When court envoy Pei Yu returned from investing the King of Min, Qian Liu sent a memorial acknowledging fault;

sentences.zh: 其子傳瓘及將佐屢為鏐上表自訴。

translations.literal: his son Chuanjin and his generals and aides repeatedly submitted memorials on Liu's behalf pleading his case.
translations.idiomatic: his son Chuanjin and his officers repeatedly memorialized on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，敕聽兩浙綱使自便。

translations.literal: On guimao an edict permitted the transport commissioners of the Two Zhe circuits to act at their discretion.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao an edict allowed the Two Zhe transport commissioners free rein.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽北院使馮贇為左衛上將軍、北都留守。

translations.literal: Feng Yun, commissioner of the northern bureau of the Palace Secretariat, was made Grand General of the Left Guard and defender of the Northern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat northern bureau commissioner Feng Yun was made Grand General of the Left Guard and defender of the Northern Capital.

sentences.zh: 丁未，族誅董光業。

translations.literal: On dingwei the entire clan of Dong Guangye was executed.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei Dong Guangye's entire clan was executed.

sentences.zh: 楚王殷寢疾，遣使詣闕，請傳位於其子希聲。

translations.literal: Prince Yin of Chu was gravely ill and sent envoys to court requesting to pass the throne to his son Xisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin of Chu lay gravely ill and sent envoys to court asking to pass the throne to his son Xisheng.

sentences.zh: 朝廷疑殷已死，辛亥，以希聲為起復武安節度使兼侍中。

translations.literal: The court suspected that Yin had already died; on xinhai Xisheng was appointed, on mourning leave from office, military governor of Wu'an and concurrent Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting Yin had already died, on xinhai the court appointed Xisheng, while still in mourning, military governor of Wu'an and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥以故蜀鎮江節度使張武為峽路行營招收討伐使，將水軍趣夔州，以左飛棹指揮使袁彥超副之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang appointed Zhang Wu, former military governor of Zhenjiang under Shu, as campaign commander for recruitment and punitive action on the Gorges route, leading the water army toward Kuizhou, with Yuan Yanchao, commander of the left flying-oar fleet, as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang made former Shu Zhenjiang governor Zhang Wu commander for the Gorges campaign, leading the fleet toward Kuizhou with left flying-oar commander Yuan Yanchao as deputy.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，東川兵陷征、合、巴、蓬、果五州。

translations.literal: On guichou Eastern Chuan troops captured the five prefectures of Zheng, He, Ba, Peng, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou Eastern Chuan forces took the five prefectures of Zheng, He, Ba, Peng, and Guo.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，吳左僕射、同平章事嚴可求卒。

translations.literal: On bingchen Yan Keqiu, Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Associate Councilor of Wu, died.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen Yan Keqiu, Wu's Left Vice Director and Associate Councilor, died.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥以其長子大將軍景通為兵部尚書、參政事，知誥將出鎮金陵故也。

translations.literal: Xu Zhihao appointed his eldest son, the great general Jingtong, Minister of War and participant in state affairs, because Zhihao was about to go out to garrison Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhihao made his eldest son, great general Jingtong, Minister of War and participant in government affairs, as Zhihao prepared to take up his post at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 漢將梁克貞入占城，取其寶貨以歸。

translations.literal: The Han general Liang Kezhen entered Champa, took its treasures and goods, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Han general Liang Kezhen invaded Champa, seized its treasure, and returned.

sentences.zh: 十一月，戊辰，張武至渝州，刺史張環降之，遂取瀘州，遣先鋒將朱偓分兵趣黔、涪。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, Zhang Wu reached Yuzhou; the prefect Zhang Huan surrendered to him; he then took Luzhou and sent the vanguard commander Zhu Wo to divide troops toward Qian and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on wuchen, Zhang Wu reached Yuzhou; prefect Zhang Huan surrendered; he then took Luzhou and sent vanguard Zhu Wo toward Qian and Fu.

sentences.zh: 己巳，楚王殷卒，遺命諸子，兄弟相繼；

translations.literal: On jisi Prince Yin of Chu died; he left instructions to his sons that brothers should succeed one another in turn;
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Prince Yin of Chu died, leaving orders that his sons should succeed one another as brothers;

sentences.zh: 置劍於祠堂，曰；

translations.literal: he placed a sword in the ancestral hall and said:
translations.idiomatic: he placed a sword in the ancestral hall and declared:

sentences.zh: 「違吾命者戮之！」

translations.literal: "Whoever disobeys my command shall be put to death!"
translations.idiomatic: "Whoever disobeys my command shall die!"

sentences.zh: 諸將議遣兵守四境，然後發喪，兵部侍郎黃損曰：「吾喪君有君，何備之有！

translations.literal: The generals discussed sending troops to guard the four borders and only then announcing the mourning; Huang Sun, Vice Minister of War, said, "We have lost a lord but gained a lord—what need is there for precautions!
translations.idiomatic: The generals debated posting troops on every border before announcing the death. Vice Minister of War Huang Sun said, "We have lost a lord but gained a lord—what is there to guard against!

sentences.zh: 宜遣使詣鄰道告終稱嗣而已。」

translations.literal: We should simply send envoys to neighboring circuits to announce the end and proclaim the succession."
translations.idiomatic: Send envoys to neighboring circuits to announce his death and proclaim the succession—that is enough."

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭入散關，階州刺史王經贄、瀘州刺史馮暉與前鋒馬步都虞候王思同、步軍都指揮使趙在禮引兵出人頭山後，過劍門之南，還襲劍門，壬申，克之，殺東川兵三千人，獲都指揮使齊彥溫，據而守之。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang entered San'guan Pass; Wang Jingzan, prefect of Jie, Feng Hui, prefect of Lu, and the vanguard chief adjutant Wang Sitong and infantry commander Zhao Zaili led troops out behind Rentou Mountain, passed south of Jianmen, turned back to strike Jianmen, and on renshen captured it, killing three thousand Eastern Chuan troops, seizing the metropolitan commander Qi Yanwen, and holding and defending the place.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang entered San'guan Pass. Jie prefect Wang Jingzan, Lu prefect Feng Hui, vanguard adjutant Wang Sitong, and infantry commander Zhao Zaili led troops around behind Rentou Mountain, passed south of Jianmen, then doubled back and seized the pass on renshen, killing three thousand Eastern Chuan soldiers, capturing commander Qi Yanwen, and holding the position.

sentences.zh: 暉，魏州人也。

translations.literal: Hui was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，弘贄等破劍州，而大軍不繼，乃焚其廬舍，取其資糧，還保劍門。

translations.literal: On jiaxu Hongshi and others captured Jian prefecture, but the great army did not follow up; they therefore burned its buildings, took its stores and grain, and returned to hold Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu Hou Hongshi and others took Jian prefecture, but the main army did not follow; they burned the buildings, seized the supplies, and fell back to Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，詔削孟知祥官爵。

translations.literal: On yihai an edict stripped Meng Zhixiang of rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai an edict stripped Meng Zhixiang of rank and title.

sentences.zh: 己卯，董璋遣使至成都告急。

translations.literal: On jimao Dong Zhang sent envoys to Chengdu to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Dong Zhang sent envoys to Chengdu pleading for aid.

sentences.zh: 知祥聞劍門失守，大懼，曰：「董公果誤我！」

translations.literal: When Zhixiang heard that Jianmen had been lost he was greatly afraid and said, "Lord Dong has indeed misled me!"
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Jianmen had fallen, Zhixiang was terrified: "Dong has ruined me after all!"

sentences.zh: 庚辰，遣牙內都指揮使李肇將兵五千赴之，戒之曰：「爾倍道兼行，先據劍州，北軍無能為也。」

translations.literal: On gengchen he sent the inner guard commander Li Zhao with five thousand troops to go to the rescue, admonishing him, "You must march by double stages; seize Jian prefecture first, and the northern army can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he sent inner guard commander Li Zhao with five thousand men, instructing him, "March day and night—seize Jian prefecture first, and the northern army will be helpless."

sentences.zh: 又遣使詣遂州，令趙廷隱將萬人會屯劍州。

translations.literal: He also sent envoys to Suizhou ordering Zhao Tingyin to lead ten thousand men to assemble and encamp at Jian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhao Tingyin at Suizhou to bring ten thousand men to concentrate at Jian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又遣故蜀永平節度使李筠將兵四千趣龍州，守要害。

translations.literal: He further sent the former Yongping military governor of Shu, Li Yun, to lead four thousand troops toward Longzhou to guard the strategic points.
translations.idiomatic: He further sent former Shu Yongping governor Li Yun with four thousand men to Longzhou to hold the critical passes.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，士卒恐懼，觀望不進，廷隱流涕諭之曰：「今北軍勢盛，汝曹不力戰卻敵，則妻子皆為人有矣。」

translations.literal: The weather was cold; the soldiers were afraid and hung back without advancing; Tingyin wept as he instructed them, "Now the northern army's power is great—if you do not fight fiercely to repel the enemy, your wives and children will all belong to others."
translations.idiomatic: The weather was bitter; the soldiers hung back in fear. Tingyin wept as he addressed them: "The northern army is strong—if you do not fight with all your might, your wives and children will belong to the enemy."

sentences.zh: 眾心乃奮。

translations.literal: The men's hearts were thereby roused.
translations.idiomatic: Their spirits rallied.

sentences.zh: 董璋自閬州將兩川兵屯木馬寨。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang led the troops of the Two Chuan from Langzhou to encamp at Muma Stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang led the combined Chuan forces from Langzhou to camp at Muma Stockade.

sentences.zh: 先是，西川牙內指揮使太谷龐福誠、昭信指揮使謝鍠屯來蘇村，聞劍門失守，相謂曰：「使北軍更得劍州，則二蜀勢危矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Pang Fucheng of Taigu, inner guard commander of Western Chuan, and Xie Heng, commander of Zhaoxin, were encamped at Laisu Village; when they heard Jianmen had fallen they said to one another, "If the northern army should also take Jian prefecture, the Two Shus will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Western Chuan inner guard commander Pang Fucheng of Taigu and Zhaoxin commander Xie Heng were camped at Laisu Village. Hearing Jianmen had fallen, they said to each other, "If the northern army also takes Jian prefecture, both Shu regions are lost."

sentences.zh: 遽引部兵千餘人間道趣劍州。

translations.literal: They immediately led more than a thousand of their troops by a hidden route toward Jian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: They immediately led more than a thousand men by a hidden path toward Jian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始至，官軍萬餘人自北山大下，會日暮，二人謀曰：「眾寡不敵，逮明則吾屬無遺矣。」

translations.literal: When they had just arrived, more than ten thousand government troops came down from North Mountain; it happened to be dusk, and the two men plotted together, saying, "We are too few to match the enemy; by dawn none of us will remain."
translations.idiomatic: They had barely arrived when more than ten thousand imperial troops poured down from North Mountain. Dusk was falling, and the two men conferred: "We are outnumbered; by dawn not one of us will be left."

sentences.zh: 福誠夜引兵數百升北山，大噪於官軍營後，鍠帥餘眾操短兵自其前急擊之；

translations.literal: That night Fucheng led several hundred men up North Mountain and raised a great clamor behind the government army's camp; Heng led the remaining troops wielding short weapons and struck them fiercely from the front;
translations.idiomatic: That night Fucheng led several hundred men up North Mountain and raised a great uproar behind the imperial camp, while Heng led the rest with short weapons in a frontal assault.

sentences.zh: 官軍大驚，空營遁去，復保劍門，十餘日不出。

translations.literal: The government army was greatly alarmed, abandoned the camp and fled, and again held Jianmen, not venturing out for more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army panicked, abandoned the camp, and fled back to Jianmen, where they stayed more than ten days without emerging.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥聞之，喜曰：「吾始謂弘贄等克劍門，逕據劍州，堅守其城，或引兵直趣梓州，董公必棄閬州奔還；

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang heard this, he said with joy, "At first I thought Hongshi and the others would take Jianmen, proceed directly to seize Jian prefecture, hold the city firm, or lead troops straight toward Zizhou—Lord Dong would surely abandon Langzhou and flee back;
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Zhixiang heard the news, he rejoiced: "I had feared Hongshi and his men would take Jianmen, march straight on Jian prefecture, hold the city, or push directly toward Zizhou—Dong would have to abandon Langzhou and flee back;

sentences.zh: 我軍失援，亦須解遂州之圍。

translations.literal: Our army would lose support, and we would also have to lift the siege of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: our army would lose its reinforcements, and we would have to raise the siege of Suizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 如此則內外受敵，兩川震動，勢可憂危；

translations.literal: Thus we would be attacked from within and without, the Two Chuan would be shaken, and the situation would be perilous;
translations.idiomatic: Then we would be attacked from within and without, both Chuan would be shaken, and the situation would grow dire;

sentences.zh: 今乃焚毀劍州，運糧東歸劍門，頓兵不進，吾事濟矣。」

translations.literal: But now they have burned Jian prefecture, transported grain eastward back to Jianmen, halted their troops without advancing—my affair is accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: but instead they burned Jian prefecture, hauled supplies back east to Jianmen, and halted without advancing. My cause is saved."

sentences.zh: 官軍分道趣文州，將襲龍州，為西川定遠指揮使潘福超、義勝都頭太原沙延祚所敗。

translations.literal: The government army divided its forces toward Wen prefecture, intending to attack Long prefecture, but was defeated by Pan Fuchao, Dingyuan commander of Western Chuan, and Sha Yanzuo of Taiyuan, company head of Yisheng.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army split its forces toward Wen prefecture, intending to strike Long prefecture, but was defeated by Pan Fuchao, Dingyuan commander of Western Chuan, and Sha Yanzuo of Taiyuan, company head of Yisheng.

sentences.zh: 甲申，張武卒於渝州；

translations.literal: On jiashen Zhang Wu died at Yuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen Zhang Wu died at Yuzhou;

sentences.zh: 知祥命袁彥超代將其兵。

translations.literal: Zhixiang ordered Yuan Yanchao to take command of his troops in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang ordered Yuan Yanchao to take command of his troops.

sentences.zh: 朱偓將至涪州，武泰節度使楊漢賓棄黔南，奔忠州；

translations.literal: Zhu Wo was about to reach Fuzhou; Yang Hanbin, military governor of Wutai, abandoned southern Qian and fled to Zhong prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Wo was approaching Fuzhou when Yang Hanbin, military governor of Wutai, abandoned southern Qian and fled to Zhong prefecture;

sentences.zh: 偓追至豐都，還取涪州。

translations.literal: Wo pursued him to Fengdu, then returned and took Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wo pursued him to Fengdu, then turned back and recovered Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 知祥以成都支使崔善權武泰留後。

translations.literal: Zhixiang appointed Cui Shan, branch commissioner of Chengdu, acting governor of Wutai.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang appointed Cui Shan, branch commissioner of Chengdu, acting governor of Wutai.

sentences.zh: 董璋遣前陵州刺史王暉將兵三千會李肇等分屯劍州南山。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang sent the former prefect of Ling, Wang Hui, with three thousand troops to join Li Zhao and the others in dividing forces and encamping on the southern mountains of Jian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang sent former Ling prefect Wang Hui with three thousand men to join Li Zhao and others in dividing their forces and encamping on the southern mountains of Jian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，馬希聲襲位，稱遺命去建國之制，復籓鎮之舊。

translations.literal: On bingxu Ma Xisheng succeeded to the position, citing a deathbed order to abolish the institution of founding a state and restore the old frontier-command system.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Ma Xisheng succeeded to power, citing a deathbed command to abolish Chu’s kingship and restore the old frontier-command arrangement.

sentences.zh: 契丹東丹王突欲自以失職，帥部曲四十人越海自登州來奔。

translations.literal: The Khitan Prince of Eastern Dan, Yelü Tuyu, believing himself to have lost his position, led forty of his followers across the sea from Deng prefecture to come and defect.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan Prince of Eastern Dan, Yelü Tuyu, believing he had lost his post, led forty followers across the sea from Deng prefecture to defect.

sentences.zh: 十二月，壬辰，石敬瑭至劍門。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Shi Jingtang reached Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on renchen, Shi Jingtang reached Jianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 乙未，進屯劍州北山；

translations.literal: On yiwei he advanced to encamp on North Mountain at Jian prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he advanced and encamped on the northern hills of Jian prefecture;

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱陳於牙城後山，李肇、王暉陳於河橋。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin deployed at the mountain behind the headquarters city; Li Zhao and Wang Hui deployed at the river bridge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin formed up on the hill behind the headquarters city; Li Zhao and Wang Hui formed up at the river bridge.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭引步兵進擊廷隱，廷隱擇善射者五百人伏敬瑭歸路，按甲待之，矛稍欲相及，乃揚旗鼓噪擊之，北軍退走，顛墜下山，俘斬百餘人。

translations.literal: Jingtang led infantry forward to attack Tingyin; Tingyin selected five hundred skilled archers to ambush along Jingtang's return route, held their armor and waited; when spear-shafts were nearly within reach, they raised flags and drums and struck with a clamor—the northern army retreated in flight, tumbling and falling down the mountain; more than a hundred were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang led infantry against Tingyin. Tingyin picked five hundred crack archers and hid them along Jingtang’s line of retreat. They held their ground until the spear-points nearly met, then raised flags and drums and charged with a shout. The northern army broke and tumbled down the slopes; more than a hundred were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭又使騎兵沖河橋，李肇以強弩射之，騎兵不能進。

translations.literal: Jingtang again sent cavalry to charge the river bridge; Li Zhao shot them with powerful crossbows, and the cavalry could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang sent cavalry to charge the river bridge, but Li Zhao drove them back with heavy crossbows and the horsemen could not get through.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，敬瑭引去，廷隱引兵躡之，與伏兵合擊，敗之。

translations.literal: At dusk Jingtang withdrew; Tingyin led troops in pursuit, combined with the ambush force, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Jingtang withdrew. Tingyin pursued, joined the ambush, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭還屯劍門。

translations.literal: Jingtang returned to encamp at Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang fell back to Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，夔州奏復取開州。

translations.literal: On guimao Qizhou memorialized that Kai prefecture had been retaken.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Qizhou reported that Kai prefecture had been recovered.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，以武安節度使馬希聲為武安、靜江節度使，加兼中書令。

translations.literal: On gengxu Ma Xisheng, military governor of Wu'an, was made military governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang, with the additional concurrent post of Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu Ma Xisheng, military governor of Wu'an, was made military governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang and additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 石敬瑭征蜀未有功，使者自軍前來，多言道險狹，進兵甚難，關右之人疲於轉餉，往往竄匿山谷，聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: Shi Jingtang's expedition against Shu had not yet achieved success; envoys from the front repeatedly reported that the roads were narrow and treacherous, that advancing troops was extremely difficult, and that the people of Guanxi were worn out from transporting supplies—they often hid in mountain valleys and banded together as robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jingtang’s campaign against Shu had not yet succeeded. Envoys from the front reported again and again that the roads were narrow and treacherous, advance was painfully slow, and the people west of the pass were exhausted by supply transport—many hid in the hills and turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 上憂之，壬子，謂近臣曰：「誰能辦吾事者！

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this; on renzi he said to his close ministers, "Who can handle my affairs for me!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply worried. On renzi he said to his close advisers, "Who can see this through for me!

sentences.zh: 吾當自行耳。」

translations.literal: I shall go myself."
translations.idiomatic: I shall go myself."

sentences.zh: 安重誨曰：「臣職忝機密，軍威不振，臣之罪也，臣請自往督戰。」

translations.literal: An Chonghui said, "Your servant's office touches upon state secrets; that military prestige has not been restored is my crime—I ask to go myself to oversee the campaign."
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui said, "I hold a post at the heart of state affairs, and if army morale has not recovered, the fault is mine. I ask to go west myself and direct the fighting."

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: The emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 重誨即拜辭，癸丑，遂行，日馳數百里。

translations.literal: Chonghui immediately took leave; on guichou he set out, traveling several hundred li per day.
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui took his leave at once. On guichou he set out, riding several hundred li a day.

sentences.zh: 西方籓鎮聞之，無不惶駭。

translations.literal: When the frontier commands of the west heard this, none failed to be seized with fear and alarm.
translations.idiomatic: When the western frontier commands heard of it, all were seized with fear.

sentences.zh: 錢帛、芻糧晝夜輦運赴利州，人畜斃踣於山谷者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Coin, silk, fodder, and grain were transported day and night by cart to Lizhou; men and livestock that collapsed dead in the mountain valleys were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Coin, silk, fodder, and grain were carted day and night to Lizhou; the men and beasts that collapsed dead in the mountain valleys were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 時上已疏重誨，石敬瑭本不欲西征，及重誨離上側，乃敢累表奏論，以為蜀不可伐，上頗然之。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor had already grown distant from Chonghui; Shi Jingtang had never wished to campaign westward, and once Chonghui left the emperor's side he dared repeatedly to submit memorials arguing that Shu could not be conquered; the emperor largely agreed.
translations.idiomatic: By then the emperor had already grown cool toward Chonghui. Shi Jingtang had never wanted this western campaign; once Chonghui left the capital, he dared send memorial after memorial arguing that Shu could not be taken, and the emperor largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 西川兵先戍夔州者千五百人，上悉縱歸。

translations.literal: Of the Western Chuan troops previously garrisoned at Qizhou, fifteen hundred in all, the emperor released them all to return home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor released all fifteen hundred Western Chuan troops previously garrisoned at Qizhou and allowed them to return home.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之下長興二年（

translations.literal: Second year of Changxing, middle and lower section of the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, styled the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (
translations.idiomatic: Second year of Changxing (931), middle and lower section of the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, styled the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (

sentences.zh: 辛卯，公元九三一年）

translations.literal: xinmao, corresponding to the year 931 CE).
translations.idiomatic: 931 CE, year xinmao).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬戌，孟知祥奉表謝。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on renxu Meng Zhixiang submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on renxu Meng Zhixiang submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 庚午，李仁罕陷遂州，夏魯奇自殺。

translations.literal: On gengwu Li Renhan captured Suizhou; Xia Luqi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Li Renhan took Suizhou; Xia Luqi killed himself.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，石敬瑭復引兵至劍州，屯於北山。

translations.literal: On guiyou Shi Jingtang again led troops to Jian prefecture and encamped on North Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou Shi Jingtang again led his army to Jian prefecture and encamped on the northern hills.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥梟夏魯奇首以示之。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang displayed Xia Luqi's severed head on a pole to show him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang displayed Xia Luqi’s severed head to intimidate him.

sentences.zh: 魯奇二子從敬瑭在軍中，泣請往取其首葬之，敬瑭曰：「知祥長者，必葬而父，豈不逾於身首異處乎！」

translations.literal: Luqi's two sons, who followed Jingtang in the army, wept and begged to go take his head and bury it; Jingtang said, "Zhixiang is a man of virtue—he will surely bury him as a father would; is that not better than having body and head lie in different places!"
translations.idiomatic: Luqi’s two sons, who were with Jingtang’s army, wept and begged to recover the head for burial. Jingtang said, "Zhixiang is a man of honor—he will surely give Luqi a proper burial. Would that not be better than having body and head lie apart?"

sentences.zh: 既而知祥果收葬之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Zhixiang indeed recovered the body and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Zhixiang did indeed recover the body and bury it properly.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭與趙廷隱戰不利，復還劍門。

translations.literal: Jingtang fought Zhao Tingyin without success and again returned to Jianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang fought Zhao Tingyin without success and withdrew again to Jianmen.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，加高從誨兼中書令。

translations.literal: On bingxu Gao Conghui was additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Gao Conghui was additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 東川歸合州於武信軍。

translations.literal: Eastern Chuan returned He prefecture to the Wuxin Army.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Chuan returned He prefecture to the Wuxin command.

sentences.zh: 初，鳳翔節度使朱弘昭諂事安重誨，連得大鎮。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhu Hongzhao, military governor of Fengxiang, had flattered and served An Chonghui and in succession obtained major commands.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhu Hongzhao, military governor of Fengxiang, had fawned on An Chonghui and in succession won major commands.

sentences.zh: 重誨過鳳翔，弘昭迎拜馬首，館於府捨，延入寢室，妻子羅拜，奉進酒食，禮甚謹。

translations.literal: When Chonghui passed through Fengxiang, Hongzhao greeted him and bowed at his horse's head, lodged him in the commandery building, ushered him into his private quarters—his wife and children bowed in a circle and presented wine and food; the courtesy was extremely meticulous.
