translations.idiomatic: When Chonghui passed through Fengxiang, Hongzhao met him and bowed at his horse’s head, lodged him in the headquarters, and ushered him into his private quarters, where his wife and children bowed in a circle and served wine and food with elaborate courtesy.

sentences.zh: 重誨為弘昭泣言：「讒人交構，幾不免，賴主上明察，得保宗族。」

translations.literal: Chonghui wept as he spoke to Hongzhao, "Slanderers plotted against me; I nearly did not escape—with the lord's clear discernment my clan was preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui wept as he told Hongzhao, "Slanderers plotted against me and I nearly did not survive; only the emperor’s clear judgment preserved my clan."

sentences.zh: 重誨既去，弘昭即奏「重誨怨望，有惡言，不可令至行營，恐奪石敬瑭兵柄。」

translations.literal: After Chonghui had departed, Hongzhao immediately memorialized, "Chonghui harbors resentment and has spoken malignantly; he must not be allowed to reach the field camp, for fear he will seize Shi Jingtang's military authority."
translations.idiomatic: After Chonghui left, Hongzhao immediately memorialized that Chonghui was resentful and had spoken ill of the court, and that he must not be allowed to reach the field camp lest he seize Shi Jingtang’s command.

sentences.zh: 又遺敬瑭書，言「重誨舉措孟浪，若至軍前，恐將士疑駭，不戰自潰，宜逆止之。」

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Jingtang, saying, "Chonghui's actions are rash; if he reaches the army front, I fear the officers and soldiers will be alarmed and suspicious and will collapse without fighting—he should be stopped in advance."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Jingtang, saying that Chonghui acted recklessly and that if he reached the front the troops might panic and collapse without fighting; he should be stopped before he arrived.

sentences.zh: 敬瑭大懼，即上言：重誨至，恐人情有變，宜急征還。」

translations.literal: Jingtang was greatly afraid and immediately submitted a report: if Chonghui arrives, he feared popular sentiment might change—they should urgently summon him back.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtang was terrified and immediately reported that if Chonghui arrived the army’s morale might turn and he should be urgently recalled.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使孟漢瓊自西方還，亦言重誨過惡，有詔召重誨還。

translations.literal: "Meng Hanqiong, Palace Secretariat commissioner, returning from the west, also spoke of Chonghui's faults; an edict was issued recalling Chonghui."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Hanqiong, Palace Secretariat commissioner, returning from the west, also reported Chonghui’s misconduct, and an edict was issued recalling him.

sentences.zh: 二月，己丑朔，石敬瑭以遂、閬既陷，糧運不繼，燒營北歸。

translations.literal: In the second month, on the first day yichou, Shi Jingtang, since Suizhou and Langzhou had both fallen and grain transport could not keep pace, burned his camps and marched north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day yichou, with Suizhou and Langzhou already fallen and supplies exhausted, Shi Jingtang burned his camps and marched north.

sentences.zh: 軍前以告孟知祥，知祥匿其書，謂趙季良曰：「北軍漸進，奈何？」

translations.literal: The front reported this to Meng Zhixiang; Zhixiang concealed the letter and said to Zhao Jiliang, "The northern army is gradually advancing—what shall we do?
translations.idiomatic: The front sent word to Meng Zhixiang. Zhixiang hid the report and said to Zhao Jiliang, "The northern army is pressing forward—what are we to do?

sentences.zh: 季良曰：「不過綿州，必遁。」

translations.literal: Jiliang said, "They will not get past Mian prefecture—they are sure to flee."
translations.idiomatic: Jiliang said, "They will not get past Mian prefecture—they are sure to run."

sentences.zh: 知祥問其故，曰：「我逸彼勞，彼懸軍千里，糧盡，能無遁乎！」

translations.literal: Zhixiang asked the reason; he said, "We are rested and they are weary; they have left their base a thousand li behind and their grain is exhausted—how could they not flee!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang asked why. He said, "We are rested and they are exhausted; their army is stranded a thousand li from home and their grain is gone—how could they not flee?"

sentences.zh: 知祥大笑，以書示之。

translations.literal: Zhixiang laughed loudly and showed him the letter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang laughed aloud and showed him the report.

sentences.zh: 安重誨至三泉，得詔亟歸；

translations.literal: An Chonghui reached Sanquan, received the edict, and hurried back;
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui reached Sanquan, received the recall edict, and hurried back;

sentences.zh: 過鳳翔，朱弘昭不內，重誨懼，馳騎而東。

translations.literal: Passing Fengxiang, Zhu Hongzhao would not admit him; Chonghui was afraid and galloped eastward on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Passing Fengxiang, Zhu Hongzhao refused to admit him. Chonghui was afraid and galloped east.

sentences.zh: 兩川兵追石敬瑭至利州，壬辰，昭武節度使李彥琦棄城走；

translations.literal: The troops of the Two Chuan pursued Shi Jingtang to Lizhou; on renchen Li Yanqi, military governor of Zhaowu, abandoned the city and fled;
translations.idiomatic: The Two Chuan armies pursued Shi Jingtang to Lizhou. On renchen Li Yanqi, military governor of Zhaowu, abandoned the city and fled;

sentences.zh: 甲午，兩川兵入利州。

translations.literal: On jiawu the Two Chuan troops entered Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu the Two Chuan armies entered Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥以趙廷隱為昭武留後，廷隱遣使密言於知祥曰：「董璋多詐，可與同憂，不可與共樂，他日必為公患。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang appointed Zhao Tingyin acting governor of Zhaowu; Tingyin sent an envoy to speak secretly to Zhixiang, saying, "Dong Zhang is full of deceit—one may share anxieties with him but not joys; someday he will surely become a trouble for you.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang made Zhao Tingyin acting governor of Zhaowu. Tingyin sent a secret message to Zhixiang: "Dong Zhang is treacherous—one may share trouble with him but not triumph; someday he will surely become your enemy.

sentences.zh: 因其至劍州勞軍，請圖之，並兩川之眾，可以得志於天下。」

translations.literal: When he comes to Jian prefecture to review the troops, I beg that we plot against him—with the combined forces of the Two Chuan one could fulfill one's ambition under heaven."
translations.idiomatic: When he comes to Jian prefecture to review the troops, ask that we seize him. With the combined strength of both Chuan, you could fulfill your ambition in the realm."

sentences.zh: 知祥不許。

translations.literal: Zhixiang did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang refused.

sentences.zh: 璋入廷隱營，留宿而去。

translations.literal: Zhang entered Tingyin's camp, stayed overnight, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang entered Tingyin’s camp, stayed the night, and left.

sentences.zh: 廷隱歎曰：「不從吾謀，禍難未已！」

translations.literal: Tingyin sighed and said, "He did not heed my plan—calamity is not yet ended!"
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin sighed and said, "He would not heed my counsel—disaster is not yet over!"

sentences.zh: 庚子，孟知祥以武信留後李仁罕為峽路行營招討使，使將水軍東略地。

translations.literal: On gengzi Meng Zhixiang appointed Li Renhan, acting governor of Wuxin, commander of the Gorge-route expeditionary headquarters, and ordered him to lead the water force eastward to seize territory.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi Meng Zhixiang made Li Renhan, acting governor of Wuxin, commander of the Gorge-route expedition and ordered him to lead the river force eastward to seize territory.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，以樞密使兼中書令安重誨為護國節度使。

translations.literal: On xinchou An Chonghui, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and concurrent Grand Councilor, was made military governor of Huguo.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou An Chonghui, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner and concurrent Grand Councilor, was made military governor of Huguo.

sentences.zh: 趙鳳言於上曰：「重誨陛下家臣，其心終不叛主，但以不能周防，為人所讒；

translations.literal: Zhao Feng said to the emperor, "Chonghui is Your Majesty's household servant—his heart in the end will not rebel against his lord; it is only that he could not guard on every side and was slandered by others;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Feng said to the emperor, "Chonghui is Your Majesty’s household servant—his heart will never turn against you. It is only that he could not guard himself on every side and was slandered;

sentences.zh: 陛下不察其心，重誨死無日矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not discern his heart, Chonghui will not live many days longer."
translations.idiomatic: if Your Majesty does not see his loyalty, Chonghui will not live long."

sentences.zh: 上以為朋黨，不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor regarded this as factionalism and was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took this for factional collusion and was displeased.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，趙廷隱、李肇自劍州引還，留兵五千戍利州。

translations.literal: On yisi Zhao Tingyin and Li Zhao withdrew from Jian prefecture, leaving five thousand troops to garrison Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Zhao Tingyin and Li Zhao withdrew from Jian prefecture, leaving five thousand men to garrison Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，董璋亦還東川，留兵三千戍果、閬。

translations.literal: On bingwu Dong Zhang also returned to Eastern Chuan, leaving three thousand troops to garrison Guo and Lang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu Dong Zhang also returned to Eastern Chuan, leaving three thousand men to garrison Guo and Lang.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，李仁罕陷忠州。

translations.literal: On dingsi Li Renhan captured Zhong prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi Li Renhan took Zhong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥欲以中書侍郎、內樞使宋齊丘為相，齊丘自以資望素淺，欲以退讓為高，謁歸洪州葬父，因入九華山，止於應天寺，啟求隱居；

translations.literal: Xu Zhigao of Wu wished to make Song Qiqiu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Inner Pivot commissioner, a councilor; Qiqiu, considering his qualifications and standing shallow, wished to make humility his distinction—he requested leave to return to Hong prefecture to bury his father, entered Jiuhua Mountain, stopped at Yingtian Temple, and petitioned to live in seclusion;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhigao of Wu wished to make Song Qiqiu, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Inner Pivot commissioner, a chief minister. Qiqiu, believing his standing too slight, sought to burnish his reputation through humility: he asked leave to return to Hong prefecture to bury his father, entered Jiuhua Mountain, lodged at Yingtian Temple, and petitioned to live in retirement;

sentences.zh: 吳主下詔征之，知誥亦以書招之，皆不至。

translations.literal: The ruler of Wu issued an edict summoning him; Zhigao also wrote to invite him—neither succeeded in bringing him.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler of Wu issued an edict summoning him, and Zhigao wrote as well—but neither could bring him back.

sentences.zh: 知誥遣其子景通自入山敦諭，齊丘始還朝，除右僕射致仕，更命應天寺曰征賢寺。

translations.literal: Zhigao sent his son Jingtong in person into the mountains to persuade him earnestly; Qiqiu then returned to court, was appointed Right Vice Director in retirement, and Yingtian Temple was renamed Zhengxian Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao sent his son Jingtong into the mountains in person to persuade him. Qiqiu then returned to court, was granted retirement as Right Vice Director, and Yingtian Temple was renamed Zhengxian, "Summoning the Worthy."

sentences.zh: 三月，己未朔，李仁罕陷萬州；

translations.literal: In the third month, on the first day jiwei, Li Renhan captured Wan prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the first day jiwei, Li Renhan took Wan prefecture;

sentences.zh: 庚申，陷雲安監。

translations.literal: On gengshen he captured the Yun'an salt monopoly.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he took the Yun'an saltworks.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，賜契丹東丹王突欲姓東丹，名慕華，以為懷化節度使，瑞、慎等州觀察使；

translations.literal: On xinyou the Khitan Prince of Eastern Dan, Yelü Tuyu, was granted the surname Dongdan and the personal name Muhua, and was made military governor of Huaihua and observation commissioner of Rui, Shen, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the Khitan Prince of Eastern Dan, Yelü Tuyu, was granted the surname Dongdan and the personal name Muhua, and was made military governor of Huaihua and observation commissioner over Rui, Shen, and other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 其部曲及先所俘契丹將惕隱等，皆賜姓名。

translations.literal: His followers and the Khitan generals previously captured, including the tiyiin, were all granted surnames and personal names.
translations.idiomatic: His followers and previously captured Khitan officers, including the tiyiin, were all granted Chinese surnames and personal names.

sentences.zh: 惕隱姓狄，名懷惠。

translations.literal: The tiyiin was granted the surname Di and the personal name Huaihui.
translations.idiomatic: The tiyiin was given the surname Di and the personal name Huaihui.

sentences.zh: 李仁罕至夔州，寧江節度使安崇阮棄鎮，與楊漢賓自均、房逃歸；

translations.literal: Li Renhan reached Qizhou; An Chongruan, military governor of Ningjiang, abandoned his command and fled homeward with Yang Hanbin from Jun and Fang;
translations.idiomatic: When Li Renhan reached Qizhou, An Chongruan, military governor of Ningjiang, abandoned his post and fled homeward with Yang Hanbin from Jun and Fang;

sentences.zh: 壬戌，仁罕陷夔州。

translations.literal: On renxu Renhan captured Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Renhan took Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 帝既解安重誨樞務，乃召李從珂，泣謂曰：「如重誨意，汝安得復見吾！」

translations.literal: The emperor, having relieved An Chonghui of his bureau duties, then summoned Li Congke and said through tears, "Had it been as Chonghui wished, how could you ever have seen me again!
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor had relieved An Chonghui of his bureau duties, he summoned Li Congke and said through tears, "Had Chonghui had his way, how could you ever have seen me again!

sentences.zh: 丙寅，以從珂為左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: On bingyin Congke was made commander of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Congke was made commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 壬申，橫海節度使、同平章事孔循卒。

translations.literal: On renshen Kong Xun, military governor of Henghai and Associate Grand Councilor, died.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Kong Xun, military governor of Henghai and Associate Grand Councilor, died.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，復以錢鏐為天下兵馬都元帥、尚父、吳越國王，遣監門上將軍張籛往諭旨，以曏日致仕，安重誨矯制也。

translations.literal: On yiyou Qian Liu was again made commander-in-chief of all armies and cavalry under heaven, Imperial Preceptor, and King of Wuyue; Supervising Gate General Zhang Kui was dispatched to convey the imperial intent—the earlier retirement had been a forged order by An Chonghui.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Qian Liu was again made commander-in-chief of all armies and cavalry, Imperial Preceptor, and King of Wuyue. Supervising Gate General Zhang Kui was sent to deliver the imperial message: the earlier order for his retirement had been forged by An Chonghui.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，以太常卿李愚為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On dinghai Li Yu, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Li Yu, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛卯，以王德妃為淑妃。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao Wang Defei was made Pure Consort.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinmao Wang Defei was made Pure Consort.

sentences.zh: 閩奉國節度使兼中書令王延稟聞閩王延鈞有疾，以次子繼升知建州留後，帥建州刺史繼雄將水軍襲福州。

translations.literal: Wang Yanbing, military governor of Fengguo in Min and concurrent Grand Councilor, hearing that the ruler of Min, Wang Yanjun, was ill, had his second son Jisheng serve as acting governor of Jian prefecture and led Jianzhou prefect Jixiong with a water force to raid Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanbing, military governor of Fengguo in Min and concurrent Grand Councilor, hearing that the ruler of Min, Wang Yanjun, was ill, put his second son Jisheng in charge as acting governor of Jian prefecture and led Jianzhou prefect Jixiong with a river force in a surprise attack on Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，延稟攻西門，繼雄攻東門；

translations.literal: On guimao Yanbing attacked the west gate and Jixiong attacked the east gate;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Yanbing attacked the west gate and Jixiong the east gate;

sentences.zh: 延鈞遣樓船指揮使王仁達將水軍拒之。

translations.literal: Yanjun sent tower-ship commander Wang Renda with a water force to oppose them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun sent tower-ship commander Wang Renda with a river force to oppose them.

sentences.zh: 仁達伏甲舟中，偽立白幟請降，繼雄喜，屏左右，登仁達舟慰撫之；

translations.literal: Renda hid armored men in his boats, falsely raised white banners to request surrender; Jixiong was pleased, dismissed his attendants, and boarded Renda's boat to comfort and reassure him;
translations.idiomatic: Renda hid armored men in his boats and falsely raised white banners to offer surrender. Jixiong was delighted, dismissed his attendants, and boarded Renda’s boat to accept his submission;

sentences.zh: 仁達斬繼雄，梟首於西門。

translations.literal: Renda beheaded Jixiong and displayed his head at the west gate.
translations.idiomatic: Renda cut down Jixiong and displayed his head at the west gate.

sentences.zh: 延稟方縱火攻城，見之，慟哭，仁達因縱兵擊之，眾潰，左右以斛舁延稟而走，甲辰，追擒之。

translations.literal: Yanbing was just setting fires and assaulting the walls; when he saw this he wailed in grief. Renda thereupon released his troops to attack them; the host collapsed in rout, and attendants carried Yanbing away in a grain bin; on jiachen he was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbing was just setting fires and storming the walls. When he saw the head he wailed in grief. Renda then unleashed his troops; the attackers broke and fled, and attendants carried Yanbing away in a grain bin. On jiachen he was pursued and captured.

sentences.zh: 延鈞見之曰：「果煩老史再下！」

translations.literal: When Yanjun saw him he said, "It truly took the Old Historian to come down again!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yanjun saw him he said, "So the Old Historian really had to come down again!"

sentences.zh: 延稟慚不能對。

translations.literal: Yanbing was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbing was ashamed and could not answer.

sentences.zh: 延鈞囚於別室，遣使者如建州招撫其黨；

translations.literal: Yanjun imprisoned him in a separate room and sent envoys to Jian prefecture to win over his faction;
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun held him under guard in a separate chamber and dispatched envoys to Jian prefecture to pacify his followers;

sentences.zh: 其黨殺使者，奉繼升及弟繼倫奔吳越。

translations.literal: His faction killed the envoys and, upholding Jisheng and his younger brother Jilun, fled to Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: His followers killed the envoys, rallied behind Jisheng and his younger brother Jilun, and fled to Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 仁達，延鈞從子也。

translations.literal: Renda was Yanjun's nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Renda was Yanjun's nephew.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽北院使趙延壽為樞密使。

translations.literal: Zhao Yanshou, northern bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat, was made Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshou, Palace Secretariat northern bureau commissioner, was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 己酉，天雄節度使、同平章事石敬瑭兼六軍諸衛副使。

translations.literal: On jiyou Shi Jingtang, military governor of Tianxiong and concurrent Grand Councilor, was additionally appointed deputy commander of the Six Armies guards.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Shi Jingtang, military governor of Tianxiong and concurrent Grand Councilor, was also made deputy commander of the Six Armies guards.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以朱弘照為宣徽南院使。

translations.literal: On xinhai Zhu Hongzhao was made southern bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Zhu Hongzhao was appointed Palace Secretariat southern bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五月，閩王延鈞斬王延稟於市，復其姓名曰周彥琛，遣其弟都教練使延政如建州撫慰吏民。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wang Yanjun of Min executed Wang Yanbing in the marketplace, restored his original name to Zhou Yanchen, and sent his younger brother Yan Zheng, chief training commissioner, to Jian prefecture to reassure officials and people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Wang Yanjun of Min had Wang Yanbing beheaded in the marketplace, restored his birth name to Zhou Yanchen, and sent his brother Yan Zheng, chief training commissioner, to Jian prefecture to reassure officials and commoners.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，罷畝稅麴錢，城中官造麴減舊半價，鄉村聽百姓自造；

translations.literal: On dingmao the per-mu tax on brewer's yeast was abolished; government-made yeast in the cities was reduced to half the former price, and in the countryside commoners were permitted to make it themselves;
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the per-mu tax on brewer's yeast was abolished; official yeast sold in the cities was cut to half the old price, and in the countryside people were allowed to brew it on their own;

sentences.zh: 民甚便之。

translations.literal: The people found this very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The people welcomed the change.

sentences.zh: 己卯，以孟漢瓊知內侍省事，充宣徽北院使。

translations.literal: On jimao Meng Hanqiong was put in charge of the Directorate of Palace Attendants and made northern bureau commissioner of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Meng Hanqiong was placed in charge of the Directorate of Palace Attendants and appointed Palace Secretariat northern bureau commissioner.

sentences.zh: 漢瓊，本趙王鎔奴也。

translations.literal: Hanqiong had originally been a slave of Zhao Wang Rong.
translations.idiomatic: Hanqiong had once been a slave of Zhao Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 時范延光、趙延壽雖為樞密使，懲安重悔以剛愎得罪，每於政事不敢可否；

translations.literal: At this time Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou were Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but mindful of how An Chonghui had fallen because of obstinacy, at every matter of state they did not dare approve or disapprove;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou were then Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, but remembering how An Chonghui had been ruined by stubbornness, they no longer dared to speak up on state affairs;

sentences.zh: 獨漢瓊與王淑妃居中用事，人皆憚之。

translations.literal: Only Hanqiong and Consort Wang held sway within the palace, and everyone feared them.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hanqiong and Consort Wang wielded power within the palace, and everyone feared them.

sentences.zh: 先是，宮中須索稍逾常度，重誨輒執奏，由是非分之求殆絕。

translations.literal: Earlier, requests from the palace had somewhat exceeded the customary measure, and Chonghui would always memorialize about them, so that improper demands had nearly ceased altogether.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, palace requisitions had begun to exceed proper bounds, but Chonghui would always report them to the throne, and improper demands had nearly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 至是，漢瓊直以中宮之命取府庫物，不復關由樞密院及三司，亦無語文書，所取不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Now Hanqiong took goods from the treasury directly on orders from the empress, no longer routing them through the Bureau of Military Affairs or the Three Departments, and without any written documentation—the quantities taken were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Now Hanqiong took goods straight from the treasury on the empress's orders, without passing through the Bureau of Military Affairs or the Three Departments and without any paperwork; what was taken were countless.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以相州刺史孟鵠為左驍衛大將軍，充三司使。

translations.literal: On xinsi Meng Hu, prefect of Xiangzhou, was made Grand General of the Left Guard and Commissioner of the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Meng Hu, prefect of Xiangzhou, was appointed Grand General of the Left Guard and Commissioner of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 昭武留後趙廷隱自成都赴利州，逾月，請兵進取興元及秦、鳳；

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin, acting governor of Zhaowu, went from Chengdu to Lizhou; after more than a month he requested troops to advance and seize Xingyuan and Qin and Feng prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin, acting governor of Zhaowu, went from Chengdu to Lizhou; after more than a month he asked for troops to take Xingyuan and the Qin and Feng prefectures;

sentences.zh: 孟知祥以兵疲民困，不許。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, citing exhausted troops and a burdened populace, did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, citing exhausted armies and a worn-out populace, refused.

sentences.zh: 護國節度使兼中書令安重誨內不自安，表請致仕；

translations.literal: An Chonghui, military governor of Huguo and concurrent Grand Councilor, felt ill at ease within and memorialized requesting retirement from office;
translations.idiomatic: An Chonghui, military governor of Huguo and concurrent Grand Councilor, grew uneasy in his own mind and memorialized asking to retire;

sentences.zh: 閏月，庚寅，制以太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on gengyin, an order directed that he retire with the title Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on gengyin, an edict ordered him to retire with the title Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 是日，其子崇贊、崇緒逃奔河中。

translations.literal: That same day his sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: That same day his sons Chongzan and Chongxu fled to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以保義節度使李從璋為護國節度使；

translations.literal: On renchen Li Congzhang, military governor of Baoyi, was made military governor of Huguo;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Li Congzhang, military governor of Baoyi, was appointed military governor of Huguo;

sentences.zh: 甲午，遣步軍指揮使藥彥稠將兵趣河中。

translations.literal: On jiawu the infantry commander Yao Yanchou was sent with troops toward Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu infantry commander Yao Yanchou was dispatched with troops toward Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 安崇贊等至河中，重誨驚曰：「汝安得來？」

translations.literal: When An Chongzan and the others reached Hezhong, Chonghui said in alarm, "How did you come here?"
translations.idiomatic: When An Chongzan and the others reached Hezhong, Chonghui exclaimed in alarm, "How did you get here?"

sentences.zh: 既而曰：「吾知之矣，此非渠意，為人所使耳。

translations.literal: After a moment he said, "I understand now—this was not their own wish; someone sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he said, "I see. This was not their own idea—they were sent by someone.

sentences.zh: 吾以死徇國，夫復何言！」

translations.literal: I will give my life for the state—what more is there to say!"
translations.idiomatic: I will die for the state—what more is there to say!"

sentences.zh: 乃執二子表送詣闕。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized the two sons and sent a memorial presenting them at court.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he seized the two sons and sent a memorial presenting them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 明日，有中使至，見重誨，慟哭久之；

translations.literal: The next day a palace envoy arrived; seeing Chonghui, he wailed for a long while;
translations.idiomatic: The next day a palace envoy arrived, and on seeing Chonghui he wept bitterly for a long time;

sentences.zh: 重誨問其故，中使曰：「人言令公有異志，朝廷已遣藥彥稠將兵至矣。」

translations.literal: Chonghui asked the reason, and the envoy said, "People say you, sir, have rebellious intent, and the court has already sent Yao Yanchou with troops."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui asked why, and the envoy said, "People say you harbor rebellious intent, and the court has already sent Yao Yanchou with troops."

sentences.zh: 重誨曰：「吾受國怨，死不足報，敢有異志，更煩國家發兵，貽主上之憂，罪益重矣。」

translations.literal: Chonghui said, "I bear the state's resentment; death would not repay it—how would I dare harbor rebellious intent? If the state were further troubled to send troops and the sovereign were given cause for worry, my guilt would only grow heavier."
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui said, "The state already bears a grudge against me; death would not repay it. How could I dare rebel? To trouble the realm with troops again and burden the sovereign with worry would only deepen my guilt."

sentences.zh: 崇贊等至陝，有詔繫獄。

translations.literal: When Chongzan and the others reached Shan, an edict had them imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzan and the others reached Shan, an edict ordered them imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 皇城使翟光鄴素惡重誨，帝遣詣河中察之，曰：「重誨果有異志則誅之。」

translations.literal: Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Imperial City, had long hated Chonghui; the emperor sent him to Hezhong to investigate, saying, "If Chonghui truly has rebellious intent, execute him."
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Guangye, commissioner of the Imperial City, had long hated Chonghui; the emperor sent him to Hezhong to investigate, saying, "If Chonghui truly harbors rebellious intent, put him to death."

sentences.zh: 光鄴至河中，李從璋以甲士圍其第，自入見重誨，拜於庭下。

translations.literal: When Guangye reached Hezhong, Li Congzhang surrounded his residence with armored soldiers, entered himself to see Chonghui, and bowed in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangye reached Hezhong, Li Congzhang surrounded his residence with armored troops, entered to see Chonghui, and bowed in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 重誨驚，降階答拜，從璋奮撾擊其首；

translations.literal: Chonghui was alarmed; he descended the steps to return the bow, and Congzhang struck his head with a mace;
translations.idiomatic: Chonghui was startled; he came down the steps to return the bow, and Congzhang struck him on the head with a mace;

sentences.zh: 妻張氏驚救，亦撾殺之。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Zhang rushed to rescue him and was also beaten to death.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Zhang rushed to save him and was beaten to death as well.

sentences.zh: 奏至，己亥，下詔，以重誨離間孟知祥、董璋、錢鏐為重誨罪，又誣其欲自擊淮南以圖兵柄，遣元隨竊二子歸本道；

translations.literal: When the report arrived, on jihai an edict was issued listing as Chonghui's crimes his sowing discord among Meng Zhixiang, Dong Zhang, and Qian Liu, and also falsely charging that he intended to campaign against Huainan himself to seize military authority, and that he had sent Yuansui to steal the two sons back to his circuit;
translations.idiomatic: When the report arrived, on jihai an edict was issued: Chonghui's crimes were said to include driving wedges between Meng Zhixiang, Dong Zhang, and Qian Liu; he was also falsely accused of planning to campaign against Huainan himself to seize military power, and of sending Yuansui to steal his two sons back to his circuit;

sentences.zh: 並二子誅之。

translations.literal: Both sons were also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Both sons were executed as well.

sentences.zh: 丙午，帝遣西川進奏官蘇願、東川軍將劉澄各還本道，諭以安重誨專命，興兵致討，今已伏辜。

translations.literal: On bingwu the emperor sent Su Yuan, Western Chuan memorial envoy, and Liu Cheng, Eastern Chuan military officer, each back to his circuit, informing them that An Chonghui had acted on unauthorized orders, raised troops for punitive action, and had now paid with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor sent Western Chuan memorial envoy Su Yuan and Eastern Chuan officer Liu Cheng each back to his circuit, explaining that An Chonghui had acted on private authority, raised troops for punitive action, and had now atoned with his life.

sentences.zh: 六月，乙丑，復以李從珂同平章事，充西都留守。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on yichou Li Congke was again made Associate Grand Councilor and defender of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on yichou Li Congke was again made Associate Grand Councilor and defender of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 丙子，命諸道均民田稅。

translations.literal: On bingzi an order was issued for equalized land taxes among the circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the court ordered equalized land taxes across the circuits.

sentences.zh: 閩王延鈞好神仙之術，道士陳守元、巫者徐彥、興盛韜共誘之作寶皇宮，極土木之盛，以守元為宮主。

translations.literal: Wang Yanjun of Min delighted in immortality arts; the Daoist Chen Shouyuan, the shaman Xu Yan, and Xingsheng Tao together enticed him to build the Precious Emperor Palace, with construction on the grandest scale, and made Shouyuan master of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanjun of Min was devoted to immortality arts; the Daoist Chen Shouyuan, the shaman Xu Yan, and Xingsheng Tao together persuaded him to build the Precious Emperor Palace on the grandest scale and made Shouyuan its master.

sentences.zh: 秋，九月，己亥，更賜東凡慕華姓名曰李贊華。

translations.literal: In autumn, the ninth month, on jihai Dong Fan Muhua was again granted the personal name Li Zanhua.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the ninth month, on jihai Dong Fan Muhua was again granted the personal name Li Zanhua.

sentences.zh: 吳鎮南節度使、同平章事徐知諫卒；

translations.literal: Xu Zhijian, military governor of Zhennan in Wu and concurrent Grand Councilor, died;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhijian, military governor of Zhennan in Wu and concurrent Grand Councilor, died;

sentences.zh: 以諸道副都統、鎮海節度使、守中書令徐知詢代之，賜爵東海郡王。

translations.literal: Xu Zhixun, deputy overall commander of the circuits, military governor of Zhenhai, and Guardian of the Secretariat, was appointed in his place and granted the title Prince of Donghai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhixun, deputy overall commander of the circuits, military governor of Zhenhai, and Guardian of the Secretariat, replaced him and was granted the title Prince of Donghai commandery.

sentences.zh: 徐知誥之召知詢入朝也，知諫豫其謀。

translations.literal: When Xu Zhihao had summoned Zhixun to court, Zhijian had taken part in the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Zhihao had summoned Zhixun to court, Zhijian had been party to the scheme.

sentences.zh: 知詢遇其喪於塗，撫棺泣曰：「弟用心如此，我亦無憾，然何面見先王於地下乎！」

translations.literal: Zhixun met the funeral procession on the road, stroked the coffin, and wept, saying, "Brother, you set your heart on this—I have no regrets, but how am I to face our late king in the nether world!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhixun met the funeral procession on the road, stroked the coffin, and wept, saying, "Brother, you set your heart on this—I have no regrets, but how can I face our late king in the underworld!"

sentences.zh: 辛丑，加樞密使范延光同平章事。

translations.literal: On xinchou Fan Yanguang, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was given the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Fan Yanguang, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was given the additional title of Associate Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，敕解縱五坊鷹隼，內外無得更進。

translations.literal: On xinhai an edict ordered the release of hawks and falcons from the Five Paddocks; neither within nor outside the palace might any more be presented.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai an edict ordered the release of hawks and falcons from the Five Paddocks; no one inside or outside the palace might present any more.

sentences.zh: 馮道曰：「陛下可謂仁及禽獸。」

translations.literal: Feng Dao said, "Your Majesty may truly be called benevolent even to birds and beasts."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao said, "Your Majesty's benevolence extends even to birds and beasts."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不然。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Not so.

sentences.zh: 朕昔嘗從武皇獵，時秋稼方熟，有獸逸入田中，遣騎取之，比及得獸，餘稼無幾。

translations.literal: In former days I once hunted with Emperor Wu; the autumn grain was just ripening when a beast bolted into the fields. Horsemen were sent after it, and by the time the beast was taken, little grain remained untrampled.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago I hunted with Emperor Wu. The autumn grain was just ripening when a beast bolted into the fields. Horsemen were sent after it, and by the time they caught it, little grain was left standing.

sentences.zh: 以是思之，獵有損無益，故不為耳。」

translations.literal: Reflecting on this, hunting does harm and no good—therefore I do not do it."
translations.idiomatic: Thinking it over, hunting does harm and no good—that is why I do not hunt."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁卯，洋州指揮使李進唐攻通州，拔之。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao Li Jintang, commander of Yang prefecture, attacked Tong prefecture and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingmao Li Jintang, commander of Yang prefecture, attacked Tong prefecture and took it.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以王延政為建州刺史。

translations.literal: On renwu Wang Yanzheng was made prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Wang Yanzheng was appointed prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of jiashen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the new moon of jiashen, there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，蘇願至成都，孟知祥聞甥姪在朝廷者皆無恙，遣使告董璋，欲與之俱上表謝罪。

translations.literal: On guisi Su Yuan reached Chengdu; Meng Zhixiang, hearing that his nephews and nieces at court were all unharmed, sent an envoy to tell Dong Zhang that he wished to submit a joint memorial of thanks and apology.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi Su Yuan reached Chengdu. Meng Zhixiang, learning that his nephews and nieces at court were all safe, sent an envoy to tell Dong Zhang that he wished to submit a joint memorial of thanks and apology.

sentences.zh: 璋怒曰：「孟公親戚皆完，固宜歸附；

translations.literal: Zhang said angrily, "Lord Meng's kin are all intact—it is only right that he should submit;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang said angrily, "Lord Meng's kin are all intact—of course he should submit;

sentences.zh: 璋已族滅，尚何謝為！

translations.literal: Zhang's clan has already been destroyed—what is there left to thank for!
translations.idiomatic: Zhang's clan has already been wiped out—what is there to thank anyone for!

sentences.zh: 詔書皆在蘇願腹中，劉澄安得豫聞，璋豈不知邪！」

translations.literal: The edicts all lie in Su Yuan's belly—how could Liu Cheng have heard of them in advance? Do you think Zhang does not know!"
translations.idiomatic: The edicts all lie in Su Yuan's belly—how could Liu Cheng have heard of them beforehand? Do you think Zhang does not know!

sentences.zh: 由是復為怨敵。

translations.literal: Thereupon they became enemies again."
translations.idiomatic: From that point they were enemies again."

sentences.zh: 乙未，李仁罕自夔州引兵還成都。

translations.literal: On yiwei Li Renhan led his troops back to Chengdu from Kuizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Li Renhan led his troops back to Chengdu from Kuizhou.

sentences.zh: 吳中書令徐知誥表稱輔政歲久，請歸老金陵；

translations.literal: Xu Zhihao, Grand Councilor of Wu, memorialized saying he had assisted in government many years and requested to retire to Jinling;
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhihao, Grand Councilor of Wu, memorialized that he had assisted in government for many years and asked to retire to Jinling;

sentences.zh: 乃以知誥為鎮海、寧國節度使，鎮金陵，餘官如故，總錄朝政如徐溫故事。

translations.literal: He was then made military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, garrisoning Jinling; his other offices remained as before, and he continued to oversee court affairs after the precedent of Xu Wen.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made military governor of Zhenhai and Ningguo, garrisoning Jinling; his other offices remained unchanged, and he continued to oversee court affairs after the precedent of Xu Wen.

sentences.zh: 以其子兵部尚書、參政事景通為司徒、同平章事，知中外左右諸軍事，留江都輔政；

translations.literal: His son Jingtong, Minister of War and participant in state affairs, was made Minister of Education and Associate Grand Councilor, placed in charge of military affairs within and without, left and right, and kept at Jiangdu to assist in government;
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingtong, Minister of War and participant in state affairs, was made Minister of Education and Associate Grand Councilor, placed in charge of military affairs at home and abroad, left and right, and kept at Jiangdu to assist in government;

sentences.zh: 以內樞使、同平章事王令謀為右僕射，兼門下侍郎；

translations.literal: Wang Lingmou, inner pivot commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lingmou, inner pivot commissioner and Associate Grand Councilor, was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 以宋齊丘為右僕射，兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu was made Right Vice Director and concurrent Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 並同平章事，兼內樞使，以佐景通。

translations.literal: Both were also Associate Grand Councilors and inner pivot commissioners, to assist Jingtong.
translations.idiomatic: Both were also made Associate Grand Councilors and inner pivot commissioners to assist Jingtong.

sentences.zh: 賜德勝節度使張崇爵清河王。

translations.literal: Zhang Chong, military governor of Desheng, was granted the title Prince of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chong, military governor of Desheng, was granted the title Prince of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 崇在廬州貪暴，州人苦之，屢嘗入朝，厚以貨結權要，由是常得還鎮，為廬州患者二十餘年。

translations.literal: Chong was greedy and brutal in Luzhou; the people suffered under him. He repeatedly entered court and lavished bribes on powerful officials, and thus was often able to return to his post—a scourge upon Luzhou for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was greedy and brutal in Luzhou, and the people suffered under him. He repeatedly came to court and lavished bribes on the powerful, and so was often able to return to his post—a plague on Luzhou for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲寅朔，初聽百姓自鑄農器並雜鐵器，每田二畝，夏秋輸農具三錢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of jiayin, commoners were for the first time permitted to cast their own farm implements and miscellaneous ironware; for every two mu of fields, three cash in farm-tool tax was submitted in summer and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the new moon of jiayin, commoners were for the first time allowed to cast their own farm tools and miscellaneous ironware; for every two mu of fields, three cash in farm-tool tax was paid in summer and autumn.

sentences.zh: 武安、靜江節度使馬希聲聞梁太祖嗜食雞，慕之，既襲位，日殺五十雞為膳；

translations.literal: Ma Xisheng, military governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang, hearing that the Founding Emperor of Liang was fond of eating chicken, emulated him; once he succeeded to the throne he slaughtered fifty chickens daily for his meals;
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xisheng, military governor of Wu'an and Jingjiang, hearing that the Founding Emperor of Liang loved chicken, emulated him; once he succeeded to the throne he slaughtered fifty chickens a day for his meals;

sentences.zh: 居喪無戚容。

translations.literal: During mourning he showed no grief.
translations.idiomatic: During mourning he showed no sign of grief.

sentences.zh: 庚申，葬武穆王於衡陽，將發引，頓食雞□鶴數盤，前吏部侍郎潘起譏之曰：「昔阮籍居喪食蒸豚；

translations.literal: On gengshen the Martial and Reverent King was buried at Hengyang; as the procession was about to set out, [Xisheng] at one sitting ate several platters of chicken [lacuna] crane. Pan Qi, former Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, mocked him, saying, "In old days Ruan Ji while in mourning ate steamed pork;
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the Martial and Reverent King was buried at Hengyang; as the procession was about to set out, Xisheng at one sitting ate several platters of chicken and crane. Pan Qi, former Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, mocked him, saying, "Long ago Ruan Ji ate steamed pork while in mourning;

sentences.zh: 何代無賢！」

translations.literal: Every age has its worthies!"
translations.idiomatic: Every age has its worthies!"

sentences.zh: 癸亥，徐知誥至金陵。

translations.literal: On guihai Xu Zhihao reached Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Xu Zhihao reached Jinling.

sentences.zh: 昭武留後趙廷隱白孟知祥以利州城塹已完，頃在劍州與牙內都指揮使李肇同功，願以昭武讓肇，知祥褒諭，不許；

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin, acting governor of Zhaowu, informed Meng Zhixiang that Lizhou's moat was now complete; he had recently shared the toil at Jian prefecture with Li Zhao, commander of the inner guards, and wished to yield Zhaowu to Zhao; Zhixiang praised and reassured him but did not permit it;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin, acting governor of Zhaowu, told Meng Zhixiang that Lizhou's moat was now complete; he had recently shared the work at Jian prefecture with Li Zhao, commander of the inner guards, and wished to yield Zhaowu to Zhao; Zhixiang praised and reassured him but would not allow it;

sentences.zh: 延隱三讓，癸酉，知祥召廷隱還成都，以肇代之。

translations.literal: Tingyin thrice declined; on guiyou Zhixiang summoned Tingyin back to Chengdu and replaced him with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin declined three times; on guiyou Zhixiang recalled Tingyin to Chengdu and replaced him with Zhao.

sentences.zh: 閩陳守元等稱寶皇之命，謂閩王延鈞曰：「苟能避位受道，當為天子六十年。」

translations.literal: In Min, Chen Shouyuan and others, speaking in the name of the Precious Emperor, told Wang Yanjun of Min, "If you can abdicate and receive the Way, you shall reign as Son of Heaven for sixty years."
translations.idiomatic: In Min, Chen Shouyuan and others, speaking in the name of the Precious Emperor, told Wang Yanjun of Min, "If you can abdicate and receive the Way, you shall reign as Son of Heaven for sixty years."

sentences.zh: 延鈞信之，丙子，命其子節度副使繼鵬權軍府事。

translations.literal: Yanjun believed them; on bingzi he ordered his son Jipeng, military governor's deputy, to manage circuit headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun believed them; on bingzi he ordered his son Jipeng, military governor's deputy, to manage circuit headquarters affairs.

sentences.zh: 延鈞避位受菉，道名玄錫。

translations.literal: Yanjun abdicated and received the register; his religious name was Xuanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun abdicated and received the Daoist register; his religious name was Xuanxi.

sentences.zh: 愛州將楊廷藝養假子三千人，圖復交州；

translations.literal: Yang Tingyi, general of Aizhou, raised three thousand foster sons and plotted to recover Jiaozhou;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tingyi, general of Aizhou, raised three thousand foster sons and plotted to recover Jiaozhou;

sentences.zh: 漢交州守將李進知之，受其賂，不以聞。

translations.literal: Li Jin, the Han garrison commander at Jiaozhou, knew of it but took his bribes and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jin, the Han garrison commander at Jiaozhou, knew of it but took bribes from him and did not report it.

sentences.zh: 是歲，廷藝舉兵圍交州，漢主遣承旨程寶將兵救之，未至，城陷。

translations.literal: That year Tingyi raised troops and besieged Jiaozhou; the ruler of Han sent Cheng Bao, chief drafter, with troops to rescue it, but before they arrived the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: That year Tingyi raised troops and besieged Jiaozhou; the ruler of Han sent Cheng Bao, chief drafter, with troops to relieve it, but before they arrived the city fell.

sentences.zh: 進逃歸，漢主殺之。

translations.literal: Jin fled back; the ruler of Han had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jin fled back and the ruler of Han had him executed.

sentences.zh: 寶圍交州，廷藝出戰，寶敗死。

translations.literal: Bao besieged Jiaozhou; Tingyi came out to fight, and Bao was defeated and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Bao besieged Jiaozhou; Tingyi came out to fight, and Bao was defeated and killed.

sentences.zh: 明宗聖德和武欽孝皇帝中之下長興三年（

translations.literal: Third year of Changxing, middle and lower section of the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, styled the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (
translations.idiomatic: Third year of Changxing (932), middle and lower section of the reign of Emperor Mingzong of Tang, styled the Sagacious, Virtuous, Harmonious, Martial, and Reverently Filial (

sentences.zh: 壬辰，公元九三二年）

translations.literal: renchen, corresponding to the year 932 CE).
translations.idiomatic: 932 CE, year renchen).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，樞密使范延光言：「自靈州至邠州方渠鎮，使臣及外國入貢者多為党項所掠，請發兵擊之。」

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Fan Yanguang, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, said, "From Lingzhou to Fangqu garrison in Binzhou, envoys and foreign tribute missions are often plundered by the Dangxiang—I request that troops be sent to strike them."
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Fan Yanguang, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, said, "From Lingzhou to Fangqu garrison in Binzhou, envoys and foreign tribute missions are often plundered by the Dangxiang—I ask that troops be sent against them."

sentences.zh: 己丑，遣靜難節度使藥彥稠、前朔方節度使康福將步騎七千討党項。

translations.literal: On jichou Yao Yanchou, military governor of Jingnan, and Kang Fu, former military governor of Shuofang, were sent with seven thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign against the Dangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Yao Yanchou, military governor of Jingnan, and Kang Fu, former military governor of Shuofang, were sent with seven thousand infantry and cavalry to campaign against the Dangxiang.

sentences.zh: 乙未，孟知祥妻福慶長公主卒。

translations.literal: On yiwei the Princess of Changqing, wife of Meng Zhixiang, died.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei the Princess of Changqing, wife of Meng Zhixiang, died.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥以朝廷恩意優厚，而董璋塞綿州路，不聽遣使入謝，與節度副使趙季良等謀，欲發使自峽江上表，掌書記李昊曰：「公不與東川謀而獨遣使，則異日負約之責在我矣。」

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang, finding the court's gracious favor generous, but with Dong Zhang blocking the Mianzhou route and refusing to allow envoys to enter to give thanks, consulted with his military governor's deputy Zhao Jiliang and others about sending an envoy up the Gorges route to submit a memorial; Chief Secretary Li Hao said, "If you do not consult Eastern Chuan but send an envoy alone, then someday the blame for breaking faith will fall on us."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang, finding the court's favor generous, but with Dong Zhang blocking the Mianzhou route and refusing to allow envoys through to give thanks, consulted with his deputy Zhao Jiliang and others about sending an envoy up the Gorges route to submit a memorial; Chief Secretary Li Hao said, "If you do not consult Eastern Chuan but send an envoy alone, someday the blame for breaking faith will fall on us."

sentences.zh: 乃復遣使語之，璋不從。

translations.literal: An envoy was again sent to speak with him, but Zhang would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy was again sent to speak with him, but Zhang would not agree.

sentences.zh: 二月，趙季良與諸將議遣昭武都監太原高彥儔將兵攻取壁州，以絕山南兵轉入山後諸州者；

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhao Jiliang and the generals discussed sending Gao Yanchou of Taiyuan, Zhaowu circuit supervisor, with troops to seize Bizhou and cut off the route by which Shannan troops might transfer into the mountainous prefectures beyond the passes;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Zhao Jiliang and the generals discussed sending Gao Yanchou of Taiyuan, Zhaowu circuit supervisor, with troops to take Bizhou and cut off the route by which Shannan troops might transfer into the prefectures beyond the mountains;

sentences.zh: 孟知祥謀於僚佐，李昊曰：「朝廷遣蘇願等西歸，未嘗報謝，今遣兵侵軼，公若不顧墳墓、甥姪，則不若傳檄舉兵直取梁、洋，安用壁州乎！」

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang consulted his staff; Li Hao said, "The court sent Su Yuan and the others back west, and we never returned thanks. Now you propose sending troops in incursion—if you do not care for your ancestral graves and your nephews and nieces, why not rather issue a manifesto and raise troops to seize directly Liang and Yang prefectures? What use is Bizhou!"
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang consulted his staff; Li Hao said, "The court sent Su Yuan and the others back west, and we never returned thanks. Now you propose sending troops in incursion—if you do not care for your ancestral graves and your nephews and nieces, why not issue a manifesto and raise troops to take Liang and Yang prefectures directly? What use is Bizhou!"

sentences.zh: 知祥乃止。

translations.literal: Zhixiang thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang thereupon dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 季良由是惡昊。

translations.literal: From this Jiliang came to hate Hao.
translations.idiomatic: From this Jiliang came to hate Hao.

sentences.zh: 辛未，初令國子監校定《九經》，雕印賣之。

translations.literal: On xinwei the Directorate of Education was for the first time ordered to collate the Nine Classics and block-print them for sale.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Directorate of Education was for the first time ordered to collate the Nine Classics and block-print them for sale.

sentences.zh: 藥彥稠等奏破党項十九族，俘二千七百人。

translations.literal: Yao Yanchou and the others reported breaking nineteen Dangxiang clans and capturing twenty-seven hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yanchou and the others reported breaking nineteen Dangxiang clans and capturing twenty-seven hundred people.

sentences.zh: 賜高從誨爵勃海王。

translations.literal: Gao Conghui was enfeoffed as Prince of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Conghui was granted the title Prince of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 吳徐知誥作禮賢院於府捨，聚圖書，延士大夫，與孫晟及海陵陳覺談議時事。

translations.literal: In Wu, Xu Zhigao established a Hall of Honored Worthies in his headquarters compound, gathered books, invited scholar-officials, and with Sun Sheng and Chen Jue of Hailing discussed affairs of the age.
translations.idiomatic: In Wu, Xu Zhigao built a Hall of Honored Worthies at his headquarters, assembled a library, invited scholar-officials, and debated current affairs with Sun Sheng and Chen Jue of Hailing.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥三遣使說董璋，以主上加禮於兩川，苟不奉表謝罪，恐復致討；

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang three times sent envoys to persuade Dong Zhang, arguing that the sovereign had extended special courtesy to the Two Chuan, and that if he did not submit a memorial confessing guilt, punitive action might again be ordered;
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang sent envoys three times to reason with Dong Zhang, warning that the emperor had shown the Two Chuan extraordinary favor and that failure to submit a memorial of apology might provoke another punitive campaign;

sentences.zh: 璋不從。

translations.literal: Zhang would not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang refused.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛丑，遣李昊詣梓州，極論利害，璋見昊，詬怒，不許。

translations.literal: In the third month, on xinchou, he dispatched Li Hao to Zizhou to argue the advantages and disadvantages to the utmost; when Zhang received Hao, he reviled him in anger and refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on xinchou, he sent Li Hao to Zizhou to plead the case at length; Dong Zhang received him with abuse and rage and would not agree.

sentences.zh: 昊還，言於知祥曰：「璋不通謀議，且有窺西川之志，公宜備之。」

translations.literal: When Hao returned, he said to Zhixiang, "Zhang will not heed counsel in concert, and moreover harbors designs on Western Chuan—you, my lord, should guard against him."
translations.idiomatic: On his return Li Hao told Zhixiang, "Dong Zhang will not heed reasoned counsel and already eyes Western Chuan—you must prepare against him."

sentences.zh: 甲辰，閩王延鈞復位。

translations.literal: On jiachen the King of Min, Yanjun, resumed the throne.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen Wang Yanjun of Min was restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 吳越武肅王錢鏐疾，謂將吏曰：「吾疾必不起，諸兒皆愚懦，誰可為帥者？」

translations.literal: Qian Liu, King Wusu of Wuyue, fell ill and said to his commanders and officials, "My illness will surely prove fatal; my sons are all dull and timid—who can be commander?"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, King Wusu of Wuyue, fell ill and told his commanders and officials, "I will not recover from this illness. My sons are all feeble and craven—who is fit to lead?"

sentences.zh: 眾泣曰：「兩鎮令公仁孝有功，孰不愛戴！」

translations.literal: The assembly wept and said, "The Lord of the Two Prefectures is benevolent, filial, and meritorious—who does not love and revere him!"
translations.idiomatic: They wept and answered, "Our Lord of the Two Prefectures is benevolent, dutiful, and proven in service—who would not follow him willingly!"

sentences.zh: 鏐乃悉出印鑰授傳瓘，曰：「將吏推爾，宜善守之。」

translations.literal: Liu thereupon produced all the seals and keys and entrusted them to Chuan Guan, saying, "The commanders and officials have chosen you—you should guard them well."
translations.idiomatic: Liu then handed over every seal and key to Chuan Guan, saying, "The officers have chosen you—guard what they entrust to you well."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「子孫善事中國，勿以易姓廢事大之禮。」

translations.literal: He also said, "Let later generations serve China faithfully; do not let a change of dynastic surname cause you to abandon the rites of serving the greater power."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Let our descendants honor the Central Court faithfully—never let a change of imperial surname in China lead you to abandon the obligations of a loyal vassal."

sentences.zh: 庚戌卒，年八十一。

translations.literal: On gengxu he died, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu he died at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘與兄弟同幄行喪，內牙指揮使擊仁章曰：「令公嗣先王霸業，將吏旦幕趨謁，當與諸公子異處。」

translations.literal: Chuan Guan observed mourning in the same pavilion as his brothers; Lu Renzhang, commander of the Inner Guard, said, "The Lord inherits the late king's hegemonic enterprise; commanders and officials from dawn to dusk hasten to audience—he should lodge apart from the other princes."
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Guan kept vigil with his brothers under one mourning canopy, until Lu Renzhang, commander of the Inner Guard, said, "Our Lord now inherits the late king's realm; officers come and go from dawn till dusk—he should not lodge with the other princes."

sentences.zh: 乃命主者更設一幄，扶傳瓘居之，告將吏曰：「自今惟謁令公，禁諸公子從者無得妄入。」

translations.literal: He then ordered the steward to set up another pavilion, helped Chuan Guan into it, and told the commanders and officials, "From now on audience is only with the Lord; the attendants of the other princes are forbidden to enter without permission."
translations.idiomatic: He had a separate canopy erected and helped Chuan Guan into it, then told the officers, "Henceforth you report only to the Lord; retainers of the other princes are forbidden entry without leave."

sentences.zh: 晝夜警衛，未嘗休息。

translations.literal: He kept guard day and night and never rested.
translations.idiomatic: He stood guard around the clock without rest.

sentences.zh: 鏐末年左右皆附傳瓘，獨仁章數以事犯之。

translations.literal: In Liu's final years those around him all attached themselves to Chuan Guan; only Renzhang repeatedly offended him over various matters.
translations.idiomatic: In Qian Liu's last years his close circle had all sided with Chuan Guan; only Lu Renzhang had repeatedly crossed him.

sentences.zh: 至是，傳瓘勞之，仁章曰：「先王在位，仁章不知事令公，今日盡節，猶事先王也。」

translations.literal: At this time Chuan Guan commended him; Renzhang said, "While the late king still reigned, Renzhang would not serve the Lord; today I exhaust my loyalty—it is still as though I serve the late king."
translations.idiomatic: Now Chuan Guan thanked him; Lu Renzhang replied, "While the late king lived I would not serve the Lord—today I give him my utmost loyalty, yet it is loyalty I still owe the late king."

sentences.zh: 傳瓘嘉歎久之。

translations.literal: Chuan Guan admired him and sighed long over it.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan Guan praised him warmly and sighed at length.

sentences.zh: 傳瓘既襲位，更名元瓘，兄弟名「傳」者皆更為「元」。

translations.literal: After Chuan Guan succeeded to the position, he changed his name to Yuan Guan; among the brothers, all whose names bore the character "Chuan" changed them to "Yuan."
translations.idiomatic: Once Chuan Guan had succeeded, he took the name Yuan Guan, and every brother whose name contained the character for "Chuan" changed it to "Yuan."

sentences.zh: 以遺命去國儀，用籓鎮法；

translations.literal: By the late king's testament he abolished the rites of an independent state and followed the procedures of a frontier command;
translations.idiomatic: By his father's dying command he set aside the ceremonial of a sovereign state and governed as a military governorship;

sentences.zh: 除民田荒絕者租稅。

translations.literal: He remitted the taxes on farmland that had fallen out of cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: He exempted abandoned fields from taxation.

sentences.zh: 命處州刺史曹仲達權知政事。

translations.literal: He ordered Cao Zhongda, prefect of Chu, to administer state affairs on an interim basis.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Cao Zhongda, prefect of Chuzhou, provisional head of government.

sentences.zh: 置擇能院，掌選舉殿最，以浙西營田副使沈崧領之。

translations.literal: He established a Bureau for Selecting Talent to oversee recruitment and performance assessment, with Shen Song, deputy commissioner for garrison-agriculture in Zhexi, placed in charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: He founded a Bureau for Selecting Talent to manage appointments and merit ratings, placing Shen Song, deputy commissioner of Zhexi garrison-agriculture, at its head.

sentences.zh: 內牙指揮使富陽劉仁𣏌及陸仁章久事，仁章性剛，仁𣏌好毀短人，皆為眾所惡。

translations.literal: Liu Renruan of Fuyang and Lu Renzhang, long-serving commanders of the Inner Guard—Renzhang was stern by nature, and Renruan loved to slander others; both were loathed by the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Inner Guard commanders Liu Renruan of Fuyang and Lu Renzhang had served for many years—Lu Renzhang was unyielding, Liu Renruan fond of defamation—and both were despised by their fellow officers.

sentences.zh: 一日，諸將共詣府門請誅之；

translations.literal: One day the generals together went to the headquarters gate requesting their execution;
translations.idiomatic: One day the generals marched together to headquarters to demand their deaths;

sentences.zh: 元瓘使從子仁俊諭之曰：「二將事先王久，吾方圖其功，汝曹乃欲逞私憾而殺之，可乎，吾為汝王，汝當稟吾命；

translations.literal: Yuan Guan had his nephew Renjun explain to them, "The two generals served the late king long; I am just now counting on their merit—yet you wish to indulge private grudges and kill them—is that permissible? I am your king; you ought to obey my orders;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Guan sent his nephew Renjun to address them: "These two officers served my father for years, and I mean to rely on their service—yet you would satisfy private spite by killing them? I am your sovereign; you must take your orders from me.

sentences.zh: 不然，吾當歸臨安以避賢路！」

translations.literal: Otherwise I shall return to Lin'an to yield the path to worthier men!"
translations.idiomatic: If not, I shall withdraw to Lin'an and leave the throne to worthier hands!"

sentences.zh: 眾懼而退。

translations.literal: The assembly feared this and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The officers withdrew in alarm.

sentences.zh: 乃以仁章為衢州刺史，仁𣏌為湖州刺史。

translations.literal: He then appointed Renzhang prefect of Qu and Renruan prefect of Hu.
translations.idiomatic: He then made Lu Renzhang prefect of Quzhou and Liu Renruan prefect of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 中外有上書告訐者，元瓘皆置不問，由是將吏輯睦。

translations.literal: Within and without the command, whenever anyone submitted memorials of accusation, Yuan Guan set them aside unread; thereby commanders and officials lived in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: When anyone inside or outside the government sent denunciations, Yuan Guan ignored them—and under that policy officers and officials kept the peace.

sentences.zh: 初，契丹捨利萴剌與惕隱皆為趙德鈞所擒，契丹屢遣使請之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Khitan captives Sheli Zhaci and the tiyin had both been taken by Zhao Dejun; the Khitan repeatedly sent envoys requesting their return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan captives Sheli Zhaci and a tiyin had both been seized by Zhao Dejun, and the Khitan court repeatedly sent envoys demanding their release.

sentences.zh: 上謀於群臣，德鈞等皆曰：「契丹所以數年不犯邊，數求和者，以此輩在南故也，縱之則邊患復生。」

translations.literal: The emperor consulted his ministers; Dejun and the others all said, "The reason the Khitan for several years have not violated the frontier and have repeatedly sought peace is that these men are held in the south; if released, border troubles will arise again."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his ministers; Dejun and others argued, "The Khitan have kept the peace and repeatedly sued for it precisely because we hold these men—release them and the frontier will burn again."

sentences.zh: 上以問冀州刺史楊檀，對曰：「萴剌，契丹之驍將，曏助王都謀危社稷，幸而擒之，陛下免其死，為賜已多。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned Yang Tan, prefect of Ji; he replied, "Zhaci is a fierce Khitan general who once aided Wang Du in plotting against the realm; fortunately he was captured—Your Majesty spared his life, which was already great favor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Yang Tan, prefect of Jizhou, who answered, "Zhaci is one of the Khitan's fiercest generals—he once helped Wang Du threaten the dynasty itself. You already spared his life, which was mercy enough.

sentences.zh: 契丹失之如喪手足。

translations.literal: The Khitan's loss of him was like losing hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: For the Khitan, losing him was like losing limb and marrow.

sentences.zh: 彼在朝廷數年，知中國虛實，若得歸，為患必深，彼才出塞，則南向發矢矣，恐悔之無及。」

translations.literal: He has spent years at court and knows the strengths and weaknesses of China; if he returns, the harm will surely be grave—the moment he passes beyond the frontier he will shoot arrows southward; I fear regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: He has spent years at your court and knows our strengths and weaknesses—send him back and the wound will run deep. The moment he crosses the frontier he will turn his bow south, and then regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 上乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 檀，沙陀人也。

translations.literal: Tan was a man of the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Tan was a Shatuo.

sentences.zh: 上欲授李贊華以河南籓鎮，群臣皆以為不可，上曰：「吾與其父約為昆弟，故贊華歸我。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Li Zanhua to a Henan military governorship; the ministers all held it impossible; the emperor said, "I pledged brotherhood with his father, and therefore Zanhua came to me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted to grant Li Zanhua a Henan military governorship; his ministers objected unanimously. The emperor said, "I swore brotherhood with his father—that is why Zanhua came to my side.

sentences.zh: 吾老矣，後世繼體之君，雖欲招之，其可致乎！」

translations.literal: I am old; later sovereigns who succeed by inheritance, even should they wish to summon him, could they bring him back!"
translations.idiomatic: I am old; future emperors who inherit this throne could never lure him here again even if they wished!"

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，癸亥，以贊華為義成節度使，為選朝士為僚屬輔之。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on guihai Zanhua was made military governor of Yicheng, and court scholars were selected as staff to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on guihai Li Zanhua was appointed military governor of Yicheng, with court scholars chosen as staff to guide him.

sentences.zh: 贊華但優遊自奉，不豫政事；

translations.literal: Zanhua merely lived at ease in self-indulgence and took no part in governance;
translations.idiomatic: Zanhua lived at leisure and stayed out of government;

sentences.zh: 上嘉之，雖時有不法亦不問，以莊宗後宮夏氏妻之。

translations.literal: the emperor commended this, and even when he occasionally acted unlawfully did not inquire; he gave him Lady Xia of the late Emperor Zhuangzong's harem in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor approved, overlooking occasional outrages, and gave him Lady Xia from Emperor Zhuangzong's inner palace as his wife.

sentences.zh: 贊華好飲人血，姬妾多刺臂以吮之；

translations.literal: Zanhua loved to drink human blood; his concubines often pricked their arms for him to suck;
translations.idiomatic: Zanhua liked to drink human blood, and his concubines often cut their arms so he could suck the blood;

sentences.zh: 婢僕小過，或抉目，或刀刲火灼；

translations.literal: for minor faults among maids and servants he sometimes gouged out eyes, sometimes carved with knives or burned with fire;
translations.idiomatic: for trifling offenses by servants he gouged out eyes or carved and burned flesh;

sentences.zh: 夏氏不忍其殘，奏離婚為尼。

translations.literal: Lady Xia could not bear his cruelty and memorialized requesting divorce to become a nun.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xia could not endure his brutality and petitioned to divorce him and take holy orders.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，加宋王從厚兼中書令。

translations.literal: On yichou Prince Song Conghou was additionally made concurrent Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Prince of Song Conghou was additionally appointed concurrent Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使董璋會諸將謀襲成都，皆曰必克；

translations.literal: Dong Zhang, military governor of Eastern Chuan, assembled his generals to plan a surprise attack on Chengdu; all said success was certain;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang of Eastern Chuan summoned his generals to plan a strike on Chengdu, and all assured him of victory;

sentences.zh: 前陵州刺史王暉曰：「劍南萬里，成都為大，時方盛夏，師出無名，必無成功。」

translations.literal: Wang Hui, former prefect of Ling, said, "Jiannan spans ten thousand li; Chengdu is its greatest stronghold—mid-summer now and the campaign lacks just cause; there can be no success."
translations.idiomatic: Former Lingzhou prefect Wang Hui warned, "All Jiannan is ten thousand li in extent and Chengdu is its heart—it's high summer and this war has no proper cause. It cannot succeed."

sentences.zh: 璋不從。

translations.literal: Zhang would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥聞之，遣馬軍都指揮使潘仁嗣將三千人詣漢州詗之。

translations.literal: When Meng Zhixiang heard of it, he sent Pan Rensi, commander of the horse armies, with three thousand men to Han prefecture to spy on the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang sent Pan Rensi, commander of the mounted forces, with three thousand men to Hanzhou to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 璋入境，破白楊林鎮，執戍將武弘禮，聲勢甚盛，知祥憂之。

translations.literal: Zhang entered the border, broke through Banyanglin garrison, captured the defending commander Wu Hongli, and his prestige was very great; Zhixiang was worried.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang crossed the border, overran Banyanglin Fort, seized the garrison commander Wu Hongli, and swept forward in force—Zhixiang was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 趙季良曰：「璋為人勇而無恩，士卒不附，城守則難克，野戰則成擒矣。

translations.literal: Zhao Jiliang said, "Zhang as a man is brave but without kindness; his soldiers do not attach themselves to him—if he holds cities he is hard to overcome; if he fights in the field he can be captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jiliang said, "Dong Zhang is brave but ruthless—his troops do not love him. Hold a city and he is hard to crack; meet him in the open and he is yours for the taking.

sentences.zh: 今不過巢穴，公之利也。

translations.literal: That he has now marched far from his own nest is to my lord's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: That he has marched out and left his base behind is already to your advantage.

sentences.zh: 璋用兵精銳皆在前鋒，公宜以贏兵誘之，以勁兵待之，始雖小衄，後必大捷。

translations.literal: Zhang's crack troops in battle are all in the vanguard; my lord should lure them with weak troops and await them with strong ones—though there may at first be a slight setback, afterward there will surely be a great victory.
translations.idiomatic: His best troops are all in the van—send weak men to bait them and strong men to strike. You may suffer a small reverse first, but the final victory will be great.

sentences.zh: 璋素有威名，今舉兵暴至，人心危懼。

translations.literal: Zhang has long had a fierce reputation; now that he has suddenly raised troops and arrived, hearts are fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang's name alone terrifies men, and his sudden invasion has set hearts trembling.

sentences.zh: 公當自出御之，以強眾心。」

translations.literal: My lord ought to go out in person to resist him, to strengthen the hearts of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: You should take the field yourself to stiffen our men's resolve."

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱以季良言為然，曰：「璋輕而無謀，舉兵必敗，當為公擒之。」

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin held Jiliang's words sound and said, "Zhang is reckless and without stratagem; when he raises troops he will surely be defeated—I shall capture him for my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin agreed and added, "Dong Zhang is rash and witless—this campaign will fail, and I will bring him in for you."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以廷隱為行營馬步軍都部署，將三萬人拒之。

translations.literal: On xinsi Tingyin was made overall commander of the campaign's horse and foot armies, leading thirty thousand men to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Zhao Tingyin was appointed overall field commander with thirty thousand men to meet the invasion.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午朔，廷隱入辭。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month, rengwu, Tingyin entered to take leave.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the rengwu new moon, Zhao Tingyin came to bid farewell before marching out.

sentences.zh: 董璋檄書至，又有遺季良、廷隱及李肇書，誣之雲，季良、廷隱與己通謀，召己令來。

translations.literal: Dong Zhang's proclamation arrived, and there were also letters sent to Jiliang, Tingyin, and Li Zhao, falsely charging that Jiliang and Tingyin were in secret collusion with him and summoning him to come.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang's manifesto arrived, along with separate letters to Zhao Jiliang, Zhao Tingyin, and Li Zhao—fabricated appeals claiming Jiliang and Tingyin were conspiring with him and inviting him to advance.

sentences.zh: 知祥以書授廷隱，廷隱不視，投之於地，曰：「不過為反間，欲令公殺副使與廷隱耳。」

translations.literal: Zhixiang handed the letter to Tingyin; Tingyin did not look at it and cast it to the ground, saying, "This is nothing but a stratagem of alienation—they wish to make my lord kill the deputy and Tingyin."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang showed the letter to Zhao Tingyin, who refused even to read it and flung it down. "A plain divide-and-rule trick," he said—"he wants you to execute your deputy and me."

sentences.zh: 再拜而行。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and marched off.

sentences.zh: 知祥曰：「事必濟矣。」

translations.literal: Zhixiang said, "The affair will surely succeed."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang said, "The matter is as good as won."

sentences.zh: 肇素不知書，視之，曰：「璋教我反耳。」

translations.literal: Zhao, who had never been literate, looked at it and said, "Zhang is telling me to rebel, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhao, who could not read, had the letter read to him and said, "Dong Zhang is inviting me to rebel."

sentences.zh: 囚其使者，然亦擁眾為自全計。

translations.literal: He imprisoned the envoy; nonetheless he also gathered troops as a plan for self-preservation.
translations.idiomatic: He detained the envoy but still massed troops to protect himself.

sentences.zh: 璋兵至漢州，潘仁嗣與戰於赤水，大敗，為璋所擒，璋遂克漢州。

translations.literal: Zhang's army reached Han prefecture; Pan Rensi fought with him at Chishui, suffered a great defeat, was captured by Zhang, and Zhang then captured Han prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang reached Hanzhou; Pan Rensi fought him at Chishui, was routed and captured, and Dong Zhang took the city.

sentences.zh: 癸未，知祥留趙季良、高敬柔守成都，自將兵八千趣漢州，至彌牟鎮，趙廷隱陳於鎮北。

translations.literal: On guiwei Zhixiang left Zhao Jiliang and Gao Jingrou to guard Chengdu, personally led eight thousand troops toward Han prefecture, reached Mimu garrison, and Zhao Tingyin formed battle lines north of the town.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei Meng Zhixiang left Zhao Jiliang and Gao Jingrou in Chengdu and led eight thousand men toward Hanzhou; at Mimu Fort Zhao Tingyin drew up north of the town.

sentences.zh: 甲申，遲明，廷隱陳於雞蹤橋，義勝定元都知兵馬使張公鐸陳於其後。

translations.literal: On jiashen, at daybreak, Tingyin formed lines at Jizong Bridge; Zhang Gongduo, military commissioner of Yisheng Dingyuan, formed lines behind him.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on jiashen Zhao Tingyin formed up at Jizong Bridge, with Zhang Gongduo, commissioner of Yisheng Dingyuan, in reserve behind him.

sentences.zh: 俄而璋望西川兵盛，退陳於武侯廟下，璋帳下驍卒大噪曰：「日中曝我輩何為，何不速戰！」

translations.literal: Shortly Zhang saw that Western Chuan's troops were numerous and withdrew his formation below Marquis Wu Temple; the fierce soldiers under Zhang's tent clamored, "What are we doing basking in the midday sun—why not fight at once!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dong Zhang saw how strong the Western Chuan host was and pulled back to Marquis Wu Temple. His crack troops bellowed, "Why must we bake in the noon sun—fight now!"

sentences.zh: 璋乃上馬。

translations.literal: Zhang then mounted his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang mounted and gave the order.

sentences.zh: 前鋒始交，東川右廂馬步都指揮使張守進降於知祥，言「璋兵盡此，無復後繼，當急擊之。」

translations.literal: When the vanguards first clashed, Zhang Shoujin, Eastern Chuan's commander of the Right Wing horse and foot, surrendered to Zhixiang, saying, "Zhang's troops are all here; there is no further reserve—you should strike urgently."
translations.idiomatic: At the first clash Zhang Shoujin, commander of Dongchuan's Right Wing, defected to Meng Zhixiang, reporting, "This is all Dong Zhang has—there is nothing behind him. Press the attack now."

sentences.zh: 知祥登高塚督戰，左明義指揮使毛重威、左衝山指揮使李瑭守雞蹤橋，皆為東川兵所殺。

translations.literal: Zhixiang from a height on a mound directed the battle; Mao Chongwei, commander of the Left Mingyi Guard, and Li Tang, commander of the Left Chongshan Guard, held Jizong Bridge and were both killed by Eastern Chuan troops.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang took a mound to direct the battle; Mao Chongwei of the Left Mingyi Guard and Li Tang of the Left Chongshan Guard held Jizong Bridge and both fell to Dongchuan troops.

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱三戰不利，牙內都指揮副使侯弘實兵亦卻，知祥懼，以馬棰指後陳。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin was unfavorable in three engagements; Deputy Commander of the Inner Guard Hou Hongshi's troops also fell back; Zhixiang was afraid and pointed with his riding crop toward the rear ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin lost three successive clashes; Deputy Inner Guard commander Hou Hongshi's men gave ground; Meng Zhixiang grew alarmed and gestured with his whip toward the reserve.

sentences.zh: 張公鐸帥眾大呼而進，東川兵大敗，死者數千人，擒東川中都指揮使元瑰、牙內副指揮使董光演等八十餘人。

translations.literal: Zhang Gongduo led the multitude forward with great shouts; Eastern Chuan's army was greatly defeated, several thousand dead; Eastern Chuan Central Commander Yuan Gui, Deputy Inner Guard Commander Dong Guangyan, and more than eighty others were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongduo led his men forward with a roar; the Dongchuan army collapsed with thousands dead; Yuan Gui, central commander of Dongchuan, Dong Guangyan, deputy inner-guard commander, and more than eighty others were taken.

sentences.zh: 璋拊膺曰：「親兵皆盡，吾何依乎！」

translations.literal: Zhang beat his breast and said, "My personal troops are all gone—on whom can I rely!"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang clutched his chest and cried, "My picked men are spent—who remains for me!"

sentences.zh: 與數騎遁去，餘眾七千人降，復得潘仁嗣。

translations.literal: With a few horsemen he fled; the remaining seven thousand surrendered, and Pan Rensi was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: He fled with a handful of horsemen; seven thousand survivors surrendered, and Pan Rensi was recovered.

sentences.zh: 知祥引兵追璋至五侯津，東川馬步都指揮使元瑰降。

translations.literal: Zhixiang led troops in pursuit of Zhang to Wuhou Ford; Yuan Gui, Eastern Chuan's commander of horse and foot, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang pursued as far as Wuhou Ford, where Dongchuan commander Yuan Gui surrendered to him.

sentences.zh: 西川兵入漢州府第，求璋不得，士卒爭璋軍資，故璋走得免。

translations.literal: Western Chuan troops entered Han prefecture's headquarters compound; unable to find Zhang, the soldiers fought over Zhang's military stores, and therefore Zhang's flight enabled his escape.
translations.idiomatic: Western Chuan troops stormed the Hanzhou prefectural compound but could not find Dong Zhang; soldiers scrambled for his supplies—and that chaos let him slip away.

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱追至赤水，又降其卒三千人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin pursued to Chishui and again accepted the surrender of three thousand of his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin pursued to Chishui and received the surrender of another three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 是夕，知祥宿雒縣，命李昊草榜諭東川吏民，及草書勞問璋，且言將如梓州詢負約之由，請見伐之罪。
