translations.literal: That evening Zhixiang lodged at Luoxian and ordered Li Hao to draft a proclamation advising Eastern Chuan's officials and people, and also to draft a letter of inquiry and consolation to Zhang, stating moreover that he would go to Zizhou to ask the reason for breaking the agreement and request leave to punish the crime of launching an invasion.
translations.idiomatic: That night Meng Zhixiang lodged at Luoxian and had Li Hao draft a proclamation to Eastern Chuan's officials and people, along with a letter of concern to Dong Zhang in which he claimed he would come to Zizhou to ask why the pact had been broken and to seek permission to punish the attack.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，知祥會廷隱於赤水，遂西還，命廷隱將兵攻梓州。

translations.literal: On yiyou Zhixiang joined Tingyin at Chishui, then returned west and ordered Tingyin to lead troops to attack Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou he joined Zhao Tingyin at Chishui, turned west, and ordered Tingyin to march on Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 璋至梓州，肩輿而入，王暉迎問曰：「太尉全軍出征，今還者無十人，何也？」

translations.literal: When Zhang reached Zizhou he entered in a sedan chair; Wang Hui came forward to ask, "Grand Marshal, the whole army went out on campaign—now fewer than ten return; how is this?"
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang reached Zizhou carried in a sedan chair. Wang Hui came out to meet him and asked, "Grand Marshal, you marched out with the whole army—how is it that not ten men return with you?"

sentences.zh: 璋涕泣不能對。

translations.literal: Zhang wept and could not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang wept and could not reply.

sentences.zh: 至府第，方食，暉與璋從子牙內都虞侯延浩帥兵三百大嗓而入。

translations.literal: When he reached the headquarters and was just eating, Wang Hui and Zhang's son's Inner Guard superintendent Yanhao led three hundred men in with a great clamor.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached headquarters and was at his meal, Wang Hui and Yanhao, inner-guard superintendent to Dong Zhang's son, burst in at the head of three hundred shouting men.

sentences.zh: 璋引妻子登城，子光嗣自殺。

translations.literal: Zhang led his wife and children up onto the wall; his son Guangsi killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Zhang fled with his family to the ramparts; his son Guangsi took his own life.

sentences.zh: 璋至北門樓，呼指揮使潘稠使討亂兵，稠引十卒登城，斬璋首，乃取光嗣首以授王暉，暉舉城迎降。

translations.literal: Zhang reached the north gate tower and called to the commander Pan Chou to suppress the mutinous troops; Chou led ten soldiers up onto the wall, beheaded Zhang, then took Guangsi's head and presented it to Wang Hui, and Hui raised the city in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At the north gate tower Dong Zhang called on Pan Chou to put down the mutineers; Pan Chou climbed the wall with ten men, struck off Dong Zhang's head, then took Guangsi's head to Wang Hui, who opened the city and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱入梓州，封府庫以待知祥。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin entered Zizhou, sealed the treasury and stores, and awaited Zhixiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin entered Zizhou, sealed treasury and stores, and waited for Meng Zhixiang.

sentences.zh: 李肇聞璋敗，始斬其使以聞。

translations.literal: When Li Zhao heard that Zhang had been defeated, only then did he behead the envoy and report it.
translations.idiomatic: Only after hearing of Dong Zhang's defeat did Li Zhao execute the envoy and report the matter.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，知祥入成都，丁亥，復將兵八千如梓州，至新都。

translations.literal: On bingxu Zhixiang entered Chengdu; on dinghai he again led eight thousand troops toward Zizhou and reached Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu Meng Zhixiang entered Chengdu; on dinghai he set out again with eight thousand men for Zizhou and reached Xindu.

sentences.zh: 趙廷隱獻董璋首。

translations.literal: Zhao Tingyin presented Dong Zhang's head.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tingyin presented Dong Zhang's head.

sentences.zh: 己丑，發玄武，趙廷隱帥東川將吏來迎。

translations.literal: On jichou he set out from Xuanwu; Zhao Tingyin led Eastern Chuan's commanders and officials to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he departed Xuanwu; Zhao Tingyin brought out Eastern Chuan's officers to welcome him.

sentences.zh: 康福奏党項鈔盜者已伏誅，餘皆降附。

translations.literal: Kang Fu reported that the Dangxiang raiders and plunderers had already been executed and the remainder had all submitted and attached themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Fu reported that Dangxiang bandits had been executed and the rest had submitted.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，孟知祥有疾，癸巳，疾甚，中門副使王處回侍左右，庖人進食，必空器而出，以安眾心。

translations.literal: On renchen Meng Zhixiang fell ill; on guisi the illness grew severe; Wang Chuhui, deputy director of the central gate, attended at his side; when the kitchen servants brought food they always carried out empty vessels, to reassure popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Meng Zhixiang took ill; by guisi he was gravely sick. Wang Chuhui, deputy keeper of the inner gate, stayed at his side; whenever cooks brought food they carried the dishes out empty again—a ruse to calm the court.

sentences.zh: 李仁罕自遂州來，趙廷隱迎於板橋；

translations.literal: Li Renhan came from Sui prefecture; Zhao Tingyin welcomed him at Banqiao;
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhan marched in from Suizhou; Zhao Tingyin met him at Banqiao Bridge;

sentences.zh: 仁罕不稱東川之功，侵侮廷隱，廷隱大怒。

translations.literal: Renhan did not acknowledge Eastern Chuan's achievements and insulted Tingyin; Tingyin was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhan refused to credit the Eastern Chuan campaign and publicly humiliated Zhao Tingyin, who burned with anger.

sentences.zh: 乙未，知祥疾瘳；

translations.literal: On yiwei Zhixiang's illness abated;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Meng Zhixiang began to recover;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，入梓州。

translations.literal: On dingyou he entered Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou he entered Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，犒賞將士，既罷，知祥謂李仁罕、趙廷隱曰：「二將誰當鎮此？」

translations.literal: On wuxu he rewarded the troops; when this was finished, Zhixiang said to Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin, "Which of you two generals should garrison this place?"
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu he rewarded the army; afterward he asked Li Renhan and Zhao Tingyin, "Which of you should govern this region?"

sentences.zh: 仁罕曰：「令公再與蜀州，亦行耳。」

translations.literal: Renhan said, "If the Lord gives me another term at Shu prefecture, that too would do."
translations.idiomatic: Li Renhan answered, "Give me Shu prefecture again and I would be satisfied."

sentences.zh: 廷隱不對。

translations.literal: Tingyin made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin said nothing in reply.

sentences.zh: 知祥愕然，退，命李昊草牒，俟二將有所推則命一人為留後，昊曰：「昔梁祖、莊宗皆兼領四鎮，今二將不讓，惟公自領之為便耳。

translations.literal: Zhixiang was startled, withdrew, and ordered Li Hao to draft a commission, intending that when the two generals should recommend someone he would appoint one as acting governor; Hao said, "In the past the Founding Ancestor of Liang and Emperor Zhuangzong both concurrently held four commands; now the two generals will not yield—only if my lord takes it himself will it be convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang was stunned and withdrew, ordering Li Hao to draft an appointment and wait until one of the two generals was recommended as acting governor. Hao said, "Liang's founding emperor and Emperor Zhuangzong each held four commands at once. These two will not yield—my lord should take Eastern Chuan yourself.

sentences.zh: 公宜亟還府，更與趙僕射議之。」

translations.literal: My lord should hurry back to your headquarters and discuss it further with Vice Director Zhao."
translations.idiomatic: Return to headquarters at once and consult Vice Director Zhao again."

sentences.zh: 己亥，契丹使者迭羅卿辭歸國，上曰：「朕志在安邊，不可不少副其求。」

translations.literal: On jihai the Khitan envoy Dieluoqing took leave to return home; the emperor said, "My aim is to secure the borders—I cannot wholly fail to meet some of their requests."
translations.idiomatic: On jihai the Khitan envoy Dieluoqing took leave to return home. The emperor said, "My aim is a secure frontier—I must grant at least part of what they ask."

sentences.zh: 乃遣萴骨捨利與之俱歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent Wan'gusheli to return with him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Wan'gusheli back with him.

sentences.zh: 契丹以不得萴剌，自是數寇雲州及振武。

translations.literal: Because the Khitan did not obtain Wanla, from this time they repeatedly raided Yunzhou and Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Denied Wanla, the Khitan from then on raided Yunzhou and Zhenwu again and again.

sentences.zh: 孟知祥命李仁罕歸遂州，留趙廷隱東川巡檢，以李昊行梓州軍府事。

translations.literal: Meng Zhixiang ordered Li Renhan to return to Suizhou, left Zhao Tingyin as inspector of Eastern Chuan, and had Li Hao administer the military headquarters at Zizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Zhixiang sent Li Renhan back to Suizhou, left Zhao Tingyin as Eastern Chuan inspector, and put Li Hao in charge of the Zizhou headquarters.

sentences.zh: 昊曰：「二虎方爭，僕不敢受命，願從公還。」

translations.literal: Hao said, "Two tigers are fighting—I dare not accept the post; I wish to return with my lord."
translations.idiomatic: Hao said, "Two tigers are at each other's throats—I dare not take the post. Let me return with you."

sentences.zh: 乃以都押牙王彥銖為東川監押。

translations.literal: Thereupon he appointed the chief adjutant Wang Yanzhen superintendent of Eastern Chuan.
translations.idiomatic: He then made chief adjutant Wang Yanzhen superintendent of Eastern Chuan.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，知祥至成都，趙廷隱尋亦引兵西還。

translations.literal: On guimao Zhixiang reached Chengdu; before long Zhao Tingyin also led his troops back west.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Zhixiang reached Chengdu; soon Zhao Tingyin marched west as well.

sentences.zh: 知祥謂李昊曰：「吾得東川，為患益深。」

translations.literal: Zhixiang said to Li Hao, "Having gained Eastern Chuan, my troubles have only grown deeper."
translations.idiomatic: Zhixiang told Li Hao, "Taking Eastern Chuan has only deepened my troubles."

sentences.zh: 昊請其故，知祥曰：「自吾發梓州，得仁罕七狀，皆云『公宜自領東川，不然諸將不服。』

translations.literal: Hao asked the reason; Zhixiang said, "Since I set out from Zizhou I have received seven memorials from Renhan, all saying, 'My lord should take Eastern Chuan yourself—otherwise the generals will not submit.
translations.idiomatic: Hao asked why. Zhixiang said, "Since I left Zizhou I have had seven letters from Renhan, all saying, 'You should take Eastern Chuan yourself—or the generals will not obey.

sentences.zh: 廷隱言『本不敢當東川，因仁罕不讓，遂有爭心耳。』

translations.literal: Tingyin said, 'I never dared to claim Eastern Chuan; because Renhan would not yield, I came to have a mind to contend.'"
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin says, 'I never wanted Eastern Chuan—but Renhan would not yield, so I grew ambitious.'"

sentences.zh: 君為我曉廷隱，復以閬州為保寧軍，益以果、蓬、渠、開四州，往鎮之。

translations.literal: You must explain this to Tingyin for me: restore Langzhou as the Baoning Army and add the four prefectures of Guo, Peng, Qu, and Kai—send him to garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Explain this to Tingyin: make Langzhou the Baoning command again, add Guo, Peng, Qu, and Kai, and send him to hold them.

sentences.zh: 吾自領東川，以絕仁罕之望。」

translations.literal: I myself will take Eastern Chuan to cut off Renhan's hopes."
translations.idiomatic: I will take Eastern Chuan myself to end Renhan's hopes."

sentences.zh: 廷隱猶不平，請與仁罕鬥，勝者為東川；

translations.literal: Tingyin was still dissatisfied and asked to fight Renhan—the victor would hold Eastern Chuan;
translations.idiomatic: Tingyin was still aggrieved and asked to duel Renhan—the winner would take Eastern Chuan;

sentences.zh: 昊深解之，乃受命。

translations.literal: Hao reasoned with him at length, and he then accepted the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Hao talked him round at length, and he accepted.

sentences.zh: 六月，以廷隱為保寧留後。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Tingyin was made acting governor of Baoning.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Zhao Tingyin was made acting governor of Baoning.

sentences.zh: 戊午，趙季良帥將吏請知祥兼鎮東川，許之。

translations.literal: On wuwu Zhao Jiliang led the officers and officials in requesting that Zhixiang additionally hold Eastern Chuan; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu Zhao Jiliang led officers and officials in asking that Zhixiang also hold Eastern Chuan; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 季良等又請知祥稱王，權行制書，賞功臣，不許。

translations.literal: Jiliang and the others also asked that Zhixiang declare himself king, exercise imperial edicts provisionally, and reward meritorious ministers; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: They also asked him to declare himself king, issue edicts on his own authority, and reward his ministers; he refused.

sentences.zh: 董璋之起兵攻知祥也，山南西道節度使王思同以聞，范延光言於上曰：「若兩川並於一賊，撫眾守險，則取之益難，宜及其交爭，早圖之。」

translations.literal: When Dong Zhang raised troops to attack Zhixiang, Wang Sitong, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, reported it; Fan Yanguang said to the emperor, "If the Two Chuan fall to one rebel who wins the hearts of the masses and holds the perilous passes, taking them will be all the harder—we should strike while they are at odds with each other and plan early."
translations.idiomatic: When Dong Zhang attacked Zhixiang, Shannan West governor Wang Sitong reported it. Fan Yanguang told the emperor, "If both Chuan regions unite under one rebel who wins his troops and holds the passes, recovery will be harder still—strike while they fight each other."

sentences.zh: 上命思同以興元之兵密規進取。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Sitong to use the troops of Xingyuan to plan a secret advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Sitong to use Xingyuan troops for a secret advance.

sentences.zh: 未幾，聞璋敗死，延光曰：「知祥雖據全蜀，然士卒皆東方人，知祥恐其思歸為變，亦欲倚朝廷之重以威其眾。

translations.literal: Before long they heard that Zhang had been defeated and died; Yanguang said, "Although Zhixiang holds all Shu, his soldiers are all men from the east; Zhixiang fears they will think of returning home and mutiny, and he also wishes to rely on the court's weight to awe his multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Zhang was defeated and dead. Yanguang said, "Zhixiang holds all Shu, but his soldiers are easterners—he fears they will yearn for home and rebel, and he wants the court's weight to awe them.

sentences.zh: 陛下不屈意撫之，彼則無從自新。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not bend your intent to comfort him, he will have no way to reform himself."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not bend to reassure him, he has no path back to loyalty."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「知祥吾故人，為人離間至此，何屈意之有！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Zhixiang is an old friend of mine—driven to this by others' sowing division—why should I bend my intent!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Zhixiang is an old friend—others drove this wedge between us. Why should I humble myself!"

sentences.zh: 乃遣供奉官李存瑰賜知祥詔曰：「董璋狐狼，自貽族滅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent the palace attendant Li Cungui to bestow an edict on Zhixiang, saying, "Dong Zhang was a fox and a wolf and brought extermination on his own clan.
translations.idiomatic: He sent palace attendant Li Cungui with an edict for Zhixiang: "Dong Zhang was a wolf in sheep's clothing and destroyed his own house.

sentences.zh: 卿丘園親戚皆保安全，所宜成家世之美名，守君臣之大節。」

translations.literal: Your kinsmen in village and garden are all kept safe—you ought to establish a fine name for your house and generation and uphold the great bond between ruler and minister."
translations.idiomatic: Your kin are all safe. Establish a fine name for your house and keep faith with your sovereign."

sentences.zh: 存瑰，克寧之子，知祥之甥也。

translations.literal: Cungui was the son of Li Kening and Zhixiang's nephew by marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Cungui was Li Kening's son and Zhixiang's nephew.

sentences.zh: 閩王廷鈞謂陳守元曰：「為我問寶皇：既為六十年天子，後當何如？」

translations.literal: The King of Min, Yanjun, said to Chen Shouyuan, "Ask the Precious Emperor for me: having been Son of Heaven for sixty years, what comes after?"
translations.idiomatic: King Yanjun of Min told Chen Shouyuan, "Ask the Precious Emperor for me: after sixty years as Son of Heaven, what comes next?"

sentences.zh: 明日，守元入曰：「昨夕奏章，得寶皇旨，當為大羅仙主。」

translations.literal: The next day Shouyuan entered and said, "Last night I submitted a memorial and received the Precious Emperor's decree: you are to become Great Lord of the Great Canopy Immortals."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Shouyuan reported, "I submitted a memorial last night. The Precious Emperor's answer: you shall become Great Lord of the Great Canopy Immortals."

sentences.zh: 徐彥等亦曰：「北廟崇順王嘗見寶皇，其言與守元同。」

translations.literal: Xu Yan and others also said, "The Chongshun King of the Northern Temple once saw the Precious Emperor; his words were the same as Shouyuan's."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yan and others added, "The Chongshun King of the Northern Temple once saw the Precious Emperor and said the same thing."

sentences.zh: 延鈞益自負，始謀稱帝。

translations.literal: Yanjun grew all the more self-important and began to plot to declare himself emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun grew more arrogant still and began plotting to declare himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 表朝廷云：「錢鏐卒，請以臣為吳越王；

translations.literal: He memorialized the court, saying, "Qian Liu has died—I ask that I be made King of Wuyue;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court: "Qian Liu is dead—make me King of Wuyue;

sentences.zh: 馬殷卒，請以臣為尚書令。」

translations.literal: Ma Yin has died—I ask that I be made Director of the Department of State Affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin is dead—make me Director of the Department of State Affairs."

sentences.zh: 朝廷不報，自是職貢遂絕。

translations.literal: The court made no reply; from this time tribute and reports ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not answer; from then on his tribute ceased.
